sentences.text: Job vacancies in the UK have seen their largest fall since the start of the year as smaller businesses cut back on recruitment, official figures indicate.
sentences.article_title: Job vacancies fall as small firms cut back on recruitment

sentences.text: Vacancies fell by 21,000 in the three months to September to 691,000, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), which said small firms were citing labour costs as a key factor in scaling back hiring.
sentences.article_title: Job vacancies fall as small firms cut back on recruitment

sentences.text: Energy costs have risen since the Iran war began, and companies have also said that increases in National Insurance and the minimum wage have made it more expensive to employ staff.
sentences.article_title: Job vacancies fall as small firms cut back on recruitment

sentences.text: The ONS figures also showed the unemployment rate fell to 4.7% in the three months to August, the lowest for more than a year.
sentences.article_title: Job vacancies fall as small firms cut back on recruitment

sentences.text: The figures are the last official snapshot of the jobs market before Chancellor John Healey presents his first Budget next week.
sentences.article_title: Job vacancies fall as small firms cut back on recruitment

sentences.text: ONS deputy director of labour market statistics, David Freeman, said the labour market remained "broadly flat", with the latest data showing the employment rate edging up and "a small drop in unemployment".
sentences.article_title: Job vacancies fall as small firms cut back on recruitment

sentences.text: "The number of workers on payroll remains slightly down over the same period, though data for the most recent month suggests that might be starting to level off," he said.
sentences.article_title: Job vacancies fall as small firms cut back on recruitment

sentences.text: Average earnings excluding bonuses rose 3.7% in the three months to August.
sentences.article_title: Job vacancies fall as small firms cut back on recruitment

sentences.text: Taking inflation into account, wages grew 0.8% in real terms.
sentences.article_title: Job vacancies fall as small firms cut back on recruitment

sentences.text: Pat McFadden, the Secretary of State for Work and Pensions, said the figures "show the resilience of our labour market" with the UK's employment rate "now the third highest in the G7, despite a backdrop of global uncertainty".
sentences.article_title: Job vacancies fall as small firms cut back on recruitment

sentences.text: However, he said that "too many young people still find themselves locked out of employment".
sentences.article_title: Job vacancies fall as small firms cut back on recruitment

sentences.text: The government is working with industry "to bring young people back into the labour market and prevent them from drifting into the welfare system", he added.
sentences.article_title: Job vacancies fall as small firms cut back on recruitment

sentences.text: The latest ONS figures showed the unemployment rate for those aged 16 to 24 was 15.6% in the June to August quarter.
sentences.article_title: Job vacancies fall as small firms cut back on recruitment

sentences.text: While that was down from 16.4% in the  March to May period, it was still higher than the rate of 14.6% seen in the June-to-August period last year.
sentences.article_title: Job vacancies fall as small firms cut back on recruitment

sentences.text: Separate ONS figures have indicated that nearly one million young people in the UK are not in education, employment or training - or "Neet" On Monday, Prime Minister Andy Burnham warned the UK faces an "economic catastrophe and moral failure" due to high levels of youth unemployment.
sentences.article_title: Job vacancies fall as small firms cut back on recruitment

sentences.text: Ashley Webb, senior UK economist for Capital Economics, said the fall in the unemployment rate was "unexpected", and that it suggests the labour market "continues to recover".
sentences.article_title: Job vacancies fall as small firms cut back on recruitment

sentences.text: But "with businesses' energy costs likely to fall only slowly, we still think hiring will stay subdued," he said.
sentences.article_title: Job vacancies fall as small firms cut back on recruitment

sentences.text: Louise Murphy, senior economist at the Resolution Foundation, said the labour market "has performed poorly in recent years as the number of jobs has fallen and pay growth weakened".
sentences.article_title: Job vacancies fall as small firms cut back on recruitment

sentences.text: But she added that the UK's "recent bout of economic resilience may finally be creating some green shoots", pointing to "rising employment levels and private sector wage growth stabilising".
sentences.article_title: Job vacancies fall as small firms cut back on recruitment

sentences.text: The quality of ONS statistics has been criticised in recent years, with a review last year finding "deep seated" issues with the body .
sentences.article_title: Job vacancies fall as small firms cut back on recruitment

sentences.text: The Labour Force Survey, which it uses to report payroll and employment figures, has suffered from low response rates.
sentences.article_title: Job vacancies fall as small firms cut back on recruitment

sentences.text: In an update on Tuesday, the ONS said that response levels had improved, but that "some volatility" remained in the statistics.

sentences.text: The families of the victims of killer Valdo Calocane had been calling for his benefits to be stopped Killers and serious sex offenders detained in hospital are among the criminals who will no longer receive benefits under proposals called for by victims' families.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: Regulations due to be laid in Parliament on Tuesday seek to end the "double provision" and prevent serious criminals receiving up to £800 a month in universal credit over several years.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: Emma Webber, the mother of Barnaby Webber, who was killed by Valdo Calocane in Nottingham and sentenced to a hospital order, said she would now "demand" ministers reallocate the funds, which she said was a "no brainer".
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: The government said closing the loophole would save an estimated tens of millions of pounds annually.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: The new regulations are expected to come into force early next year, subject to parliamentary approval.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: Currently, serious criminals on hospital orders - where their bed and board is funded by the NHS - continue to receive any benefits they were paid on the outside.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: Students Barnaby and Grace O'Malley-Kumar, and caretaker Ian Coates, were stabbed to death on 13 June 2023 by Calocane, who had been diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia in 2020.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: Calocane was convicted of manslaughter on the basis of diminished responsibility, and detained at a high-security hospital.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: The parents of Barnaby and Grace met with Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden to discuss the change on Monday.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: Emma Webber said the move was "long overdue".
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: Barnaby Webber, Grace O'Malley-Kumar and Ian Coates were killed in the Nottingham attacks Webber told the BBC it was "not an insignificant amount of money - but it is not just the money".
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: "These criminal patients, who have devastated lives as well as taken lives [are] not only having their full bed and board and all of their care and rehabilitation provided for them, but also amassing a small fortune while they're inside.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: "The rest of us on the outside are desperately trying to survive and find a way forward in our lives." Webber said she believed the funds should be directed to the victims of serious crime so families "are given the support and the advocacy they need".
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: She added when her son was killed, her family was allocated a support worker who had 50 other families to look after.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: Webber said: "I beg and I plead, and - actually, I demand - ministers now consider the appropriate reuse of those funds." Dr Sanjoy Kumar, Grace's father, said: "Our campaign has always been about accountability and fairness.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: "Offenders with treatment orders already cost the taxpayer an enormous amount.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: "On release, every offender gets help with housing and benefits.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: Tape was given a hospital order detaining him indefinitely after he pleaded guilty to manslaughter by reason of diminished responsibility.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: Kennedi's mother Linda Westcarr said: "For many victims' families, the question of whether serious offenders should continue to receive benefits raises understandable concerns about fairness, accountability and the values we uphold as a society.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: McFadden said: "We said we'd act to tackle this gross unfairness and we're delivering on that promise.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: "For too long these violent criminals have had their living costs paid by the taxpayer twice over, while their victims and families paid the price.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: "That ends today because victims and taxpayers deserve a system that is fair and supports only those who genuinely need it." Housing, communities and local government secretary Angela Rayner said she paid tribute to the families who had campaigned on the matter.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: She added: "I'm aware the secretary of state has met with the families regarding this and was quite frankly astonished that the situation was as it was, and that these people were receiving benefits.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: "That's why the secretary of state has taken this action and I welcome it." She added that the reallocation of funds was "something for the chancellor and secretary of state".
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: Shadow Work and Pensions Secretary Helen Whately said: "Killers and rapists should not pocket benefits from a hospital bed.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: "Labour has taken all year to stop a loophole it promised to close.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: And tens of millions saved barely makes a dent in the benefits bill Labour has let spiral out of control.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: The offences covered include manslaughter, attempted murder, wounding with intent to cause grievous bodily harm, rape, assault by penetration and rape of a child under 13.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: Murder is not included because a hospital order is not an available sentence for the offence.
sentences.article_title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits

sentences.text: Monica is the founder of charity Women's Health Hope This report contains detailed descriptions of medical symptoms.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: Monica Thomas was in her teens when she started experiencing intimate itching and soreness, but despite numerous trips to the doctors it was dismissed as thrush.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: Her symptoms got worse, with sores and blisters leaving her in constant pain.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: "I was bed bound for quite a long time because I couldn't walk," she says.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: Monica says she was examined 28 times in six months before being offered a biopsy.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: She says "we don't really talk about" gynaecological health as a society so there is a taboo around speaking about symptoms.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: "Even when we go to the doctors, for me, the embarrassment of having to get undressed...with these doctors looking it is embarrassing," she says.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: "But equally when you're in pain or it's itching and you've got discomfort, living with it is just as bad." The 34-year-old from Suffolk was eventually diagnosed with a condition called lichen sclerosus.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: Dr Nighat Arif is author of The Knowledge: Your guide to female health – from menstruation to the menopause The lifelong inflammatory condition affects genitals and can cause white patches to form with itching, soreness, splitting and tears, says Dr Nighat Arif, a GP specialising in women's health.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: It affects men and women but is more common in women over 50 , external .
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: There is also a small risk of vulval cancer. , external "It's very sore to have sexual intercourse, to pass urine and it gets mixed up with sexually transmitted diseases but it's not contagious," she tells BBC Radio 5 Live podcast That Time of the Month .
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: Research into the prevalence of vulval lichen sclerosus is limited but analysis by the University of Bristol of people in the West Midlands and Warwickshire estimated it affects about 1% of women.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: Dr Sophie Rees, who helped conduct the research, tells the BBC: "This is almost certainly an underestimate, as we know that there is often a very long delay to diagnosis, and some people probably go their entire lives undiagnosed.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: "There is unfortunately a lot of shame and embarrassment around seeking help for vulval symptoms, as well as a lack of awareness, even amongst healthcare professionals." She adds: "More research is badly needed into true prevalence." Monica says multiple misdiagnoses had a "significant" impact on her mental health.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: "I didn't know how to go on... with having no answer, it was just a horrific,  lonely time." She was given medication for herpes.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: "I was very upset in an appointment with a dermatologist who got quite angry with me because I was like, 'it's not that'.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: "Then she said that she wanted me to have blood tests for HIV." Doctors told her she was "too young" to have lichen sclerosus.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: "But sadly, women do have it at all ages, you can have it as a child.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: So I found that really quite difficult, but I always knew that it wasn't right." What is lichen sclerosus?
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: Monica believes there should be more support for those with lichen sclerosus.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: "Once you have a diagnosis, you're still necessarily not treated in the manner that you should, I don't even get a checkup," she says.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: "I manage it on my own with my steroid cream and hope that I'm doing everything right." According to the NHS website, , external the cause of lichen sclerosus is unknown.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: It might be caused by the immune system mistakenly attacking and damaging your skin.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: It is not contagious, caused by an infection or by poor personal hygiene.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: Rubbing or damage to the skin can trigger the condition or make it worse.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: Clare urged anyone with any symptoms to make sure they were examined by a doctor Clare Baumhaeur, 53, from Kent first experienced symptoms aged five.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: "I was itchy and I was sore, and I was always told off, I wasn't obviously aware what was going on." Her symptoms worsened into adulthood with tears, blisters and sores.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: "But you don't see other vulvas, so I had no idea mine wasn't normal.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: I'd had in that time eight smear tests as well and nothing was ever said." In 2016 Clare experienced a tear which did not heal.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: "I was 43 that year, having it for 38 years at that point, I just couldn't take it any more." A GP told Clare she had herpes and to go to a sexual health clinic, she says she was "shocked" as she had been married for 25 years.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: She was eventually referred for a biopsy and was diagnosed with lichen sclerosus and vulval cancer.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: "I'd never heard of lichen sclerosus and also I had a cancer that I'd ever heard of in a place I'd never heard of.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: "That was the first time I heard the word vulva, no health professional had mentioned it, so it was a lot to take in at that time." Clare had been in remission from vulval cancer for seven years, when a regular check-up revealed a cancer recurrence and she underwent surgery three years ago.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: In June another check up found pre-cancerous cells and she had a sixth surgery.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: Clare believes if she had been diagnosed with lichen sclerosus earlier, her cancer may have been diagnosed before it got to stage three.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: "I had to have radiotherapy twice and that's left me with instant early menopause, lymphoedema and nerve damage." Monica encourages women experiencing any changes to their body to keep a diary.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: "It's really important that we get to know our bodies better, to know what's normal for you in your private parts as well, because actually our vulvas do change.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: "If you are being dismissed, get multiple opinions, just keep going back because you don't have to live without answers." She recommended the Lichen Sclerosus Guide , external which has a diagram and template to help you talk to doctors.
sentences.article_title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about

sentences.text: The US growth rate has been faster than was forecast by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) , external in the immediate wake of Trump's announcement of a swathe of new tariffs on goods coming into the US on 2 April 2025.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: It downgraded its forecasts at the time, citing the negative impact of Trump's import duties on investment and consumer spending.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: Though it is important to note that Trump eased the tariffs considerably in the months that followed, reducing the impact that had initially been expected on the economy.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The US economy has also been heavily supported in recent years by American technology companies making massive investments in AI, including by constructing data centres around the country.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: Spending on building data centres , external (excluding the IT hardware to go in them) by US businesses in August 2026 was $5bn, almost double the monthly rate when Trump returned to office.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: Many American voters wanted to punish Joe Biden in the 2024 presidential election, holding him responsible for the pain caused by a significant spike in prices in the wake of the pandemic.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The current rate of US inflation , external is 3.7%.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: That's still well down on the recent peak rate of 9% under Biden in 2022, but higher than the 3% rate that Donald Trump inherited in January 2025.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: Economists estimate , external US inflation would have been lower without the new tariffs imposed by Trump since he returned to office.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: While the impact of the Iran war on global energy prices, with the significant disruption to oil and fuel supplies from the Middle East, has also helped push up US domestic inflation.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The price of a gallon of diesel in the US , external - a fuel used not only by drivers but also widely in agriculture and industry - hit a record high of $6.52 in September.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The price of some grocery staples , external like beef and coffee have risen since Trump returned to office, though the price of eggs has fallen.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: And some US retailers have warned , external that rising energy prices caused by the Iran war will make producing food more expensive and raise prices at the till.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: Average US household incomes are still rising under Trump.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The median income - after adjusting for inflation - rose 2.6% in 2025 to $87,460, the highest on record , external .
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The richest 1%, by contrast, are estimated to be an average of $12,560 better off than they woud have been, primarily because of Trump's tax cuts.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: ITEP's estimates about the impact of tariffs on American households of different income levels are broadly similar to those of the Tax Foundation think tank , external .
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: Trump predicted his tariffs would result in America being "flooded with jobs" , external as manufacturing firms set up new factories on US soil to avoid their products being taxed at the border.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: Since he returned to the White House, an average of 34,000 jobs have been added to the economy each month. ​​But that is significantly down on the 122,000 jobs added each month in the final year of Biden's presidency , external .
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: And the number of Americans employed in manufacturing , external - 12.6 million in September 2026 - is slightly lower than it was when Trump's second term began.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: However, the US unemployment rate remains relatively low , external at 4.2%, which is broadly where it was when Trump returned to the White House.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: Part of the reason for this is Trump's immigration crackdown and deportation programme, which has reduced the size of the available US workforce , external and means a lower number of jobs need to be created each month to stop unemployment rising.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: US government borrowing has increased in Trump's second term, partly driven up by his significant tax cuts .
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The federal government deficit - the gap between its revenues from taxes and its spending - was $2 trillion in the year to September 2026 , external .
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: That's equivalent to around 6% , external of US GDP.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: And the US deficit is projected to rise to above 8% of GDP by 2030 , external .
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: That high rate of government borrowing is itself helping to boost US GDP growth.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The IMF has warned that excessive US government borrowing , external , which it uses to bridge the deficit, and its rapidly rising national debt are raising the risk of a future financial crisis in America.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: This would have a deeply damaging impact on most American households.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The growing deficit is also one of the reasons the US government gets charged more to borrow money in financial markets.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The 10-year US government bond yield has risen sharply since Trump returned to office in January 2025 and is now above 5%, the highest rate since the global financial crisis in 2007.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: That increase in the market cost of US government borrowing also puts upward pressure on the interest rates on mortgages available to American households.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The interest rate on a new 30-year US mortgage has risen to 7.4% , external per year, up from 6.9% when Trump returned to the White House.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: That's added to problems in the US housing market, making homes less affordable for new buyers.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: It has left many existing owners reluctant to move because doing so would mean giving up their cheaper mortgages, which they took out at lower rates , external and cannot take with them to a new property.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: Olivia says she chose to attend this dating event because she has "app fatigue" Checking in at a dating event in a bar in Guildford, Olivia Miller-Davis is understandably apprehensive.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: Even bringing a friend with her doesn't remove the awkwardness at the start of the night.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: "It's always nerve-wracking when you're meeting new people," the 28-year-old admits before downloading an app that will match her to other daters based on their star signs.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: This is speed dating 2026-style and Olivia, like many people we speak to, is here because she's fed up of "endlessly swiping" or as some describe it "app fatigue".
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: She says she hates judging people with "really limited information and just a couple of pictures" because she doesn't feel she can "really fully commit" with so little to go on.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: According to a recent study from online regulator Ofcom 11% of adults use dating sites but it suggests the time we spend on them is dropping, from a peak of almost four hours a month in 2023, down to three hours last year.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: Edward believes apps are designed so you don't actually find "the one" Olivia's first match on the night is Edward and he agrees that recent dating trends leave him feeling cold.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: "I'm fed up with apps," he says.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: "I mean, they're designed so that you don't find 'the one', because they want you to come back and use the app forever.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: They don't want you to get married from the app." The event is organised by Love at First Sign, a dating company that uses an app to match people based on astrological connection, but most people are just using it as an icebreaker.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: Director of events Lissy Cleminson says the way people date is changing and a big factor is more home working since Covid, which means people do not meet in offices or on the commute.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: "The little meet-cutes don't happen so much when you're at home with your shirt up top and your pyjamas down bottom," she jokes.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: This video can not be played As you may expect at a dating event many of the singles told us they were keen for that in-real-life or IRL experience.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: There are a lot of #SingleTok and #Singlelife accounts on TikTok and Instagram reviewing dating events.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: Candice Gallagher runs an account called @Candilicious and recently went to 10 different dating events in 10 weeks.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: She describes herself as an entrepreneur and thinks in business terms dating events deliver "much greater return on investment".
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: The 40-year-old says all too often dating online can lead to "chat graveyards" with very limited conversation.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: These events typically cost around £15 to £30 and often include a drink and activity or icebreaking gimmick, in this case an app that is used throughout the night.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: Olivia believes money plays a big factor in dating.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: "I wasn't working for a bit because I changed careers and because of that I put dating on hold." Olivia remembers thinking it "couldn't be a priority" and feeling she needed to wait until she was "earning enough" before dating again.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: She is not alone in finding dating expensive.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: More than a quarter of daters surveyed by Barclays suggested rising costs had changed how they date.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: And a couple of recent studies suggest the monthly cost of dating - from apps to entertainment and clothes - can add up to around £130.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: Many people at the event in Guildford agreed dating events were better value for money Those running apps are quick to point out online is still a big part in the way people meet.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: New research from Match Group, which owns Tinder and Hinge, suggests that out of those who had ever had a romantic relationship, about 21% of baby boomers surveyed met their most recent partner at a pub, bar or club.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: Among Gen Z, it was just 4%.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: The survey of 3,007 single people also suggests that of those who had ever had a relationship, 20% met their most recent partner on a dating app and 20% met through friends.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: Chine Mmegwa, head of strategy, corporate development and operations at Match Group, said Tinder has made tweaks to its service in the past year to win back younger daters.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: As well as helping users find out more about each other in advance of dates, through interactive music and astrology features, it has introduced "double date mode" for friends who want to date together.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: And she said Tinder is doing more to encourage people to connect IRL.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: "They want to be in person.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: You've seen us launch events across the US and now the UK.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: We are bringing IRL experiences into the app.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: "What we're doing is putting IRL into our experience.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: And so we are bringing that gap to what they're looking for in person, using the apps." In Guildford, Olivia says her night was a success because she met some men she might want to go on a first date with.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: When pushed by the BBC on whether she thought she had met "the one", she laughs and becomes understandably guarded.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: "No, I'm not going to name anyone specific.
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: But you'll be invited to the wedding if there is one!" I've been with my boyfriend for two years and don't know his salary 'I'd be put off if he asked to split it': Who should pay on a first date?
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: My friends always want to split the bill equally, how do I say no?
sentences.article_title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Spacecraft heading to Mars' moon Phobos lifts off from Japan A spacecraft has launched from Japan headed for Mars' moon Phobos, where it will attempt to grab some moondust and bring it back to Earth.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: If it is successful, this will become the first time a sample has been returned from Mars or its moons to be analysed in laboratories here on Earth.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: The spacecraft is scheduled to arrive at Phobos in August 2027.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: It is hoped that the Mars Moons Exploration (MMX) mission, which is led by the Japanese Space Agency, will solve the mystery of how Mars's moons formed.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Prof Sara Russell, from the Natural History Museum, who is the MMX mission's deputy for sample analysis, said: "There hasn't yet been a successful mission to go to Phobos and bring a bit back to Earth.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "I think this is an incredibly ambitious and fun mission," she said.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: There are only three moons in the inner Solar System: our own Moon, and two around Mars, which are called Phobos and Deimos.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Both of these are tiny - Phobos is about 20km (12 miles) across and Deimos is about 10km (six miles) across.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: They are also irregularly shaped, looking a bit like space potatoes.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: The MMX spacecraft will study Deimos as it arrives in the Mars neighbourhood, and then will focus on Phobos.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: It plans to set down a small rover to explore the terrain, though this will be no easy feat.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Sara Russell says no one has ever landed a rover on such a small moon.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "The moon itself doesn't have very much of its own gravity," she explained.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "But it's next to an enormous planet that's got a much higher gravity,  and that makes it much harder to get a rover onto the surface." Mars got its moons about 4.5bn years ago - but no one knows how they formed The rover will scout out a landing site so that the MMX spacecraft itself can later touch down on Phobos.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Once on the surface, it will deploy a robotic arm and two samplers to grab some moon dust.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: This material will be packed into a small capsule that will return to Earth in 2031, landing in the Woomera desert of South Australia.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: The amount of material that will come back is tiny - just 10g.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "It's a very small [amount] actually," said Dr Chrysa Avdellidou, from Leicester University, who is working with the Japanese mission.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "However we can do several studies even on individual grains… You don't need to have kilos back from a surface in order to do science.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: So it's worth every gram," she said.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: The spacecraft will collect 10g of moon dust from the surface of Phobos Scientists believe the sample will finally shed light on the puzzle of where Mars's moons came from.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: There are two competing ideas.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Either a space rock smashed into Mars early in its history, and Phobos and Deimos were created from the debris.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Or the moons are two wandering asteroids from the outer Solar System, which were grabbed by the Red Planet's gravity.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "When we get the sample back, we'll be able to look in detail at its chemistry and its mineral composition - and the two hypotheses will produce very distinct results," said Sara Russell.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "It should be pretty much immediately obvious.. whether it's the product of this dramatic impact or whether it's a captured asteroid.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: So we'll find that out really quickly." The team is also hoping there might be an extra bonus coming back to their labs.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "One of the really exciting things is that Phobos is so close to the Mars surface that whenever there's an impact into the Mars surface, little grains might actually become implanted into Phobos itself," said Russell.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "And that means that the sample we get back may actually contain grains of Mars as well.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: So it can give us really direct information about the composition and history of Mars." Martian meteorites are rare - this one is on display at the Natural History Museum Bringing material from Mars back to Earth has long been an ambition of space scientists.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: The Nasa Perseverance rover, which has been exploring Mars since 2021, has been carefully collecting samples on Mars and storing them in canisters.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: But a second Nasa/ESA mission, called Mars Sample Return, that would have picked up and returned these canisters, has been effectively cancelled, after its funding was halted by the US Congress.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: China is planning its own sampling mission to Mars, set to launch in 2028.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: It will attempt to return Martian material to Earth in 2031.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: We do already have some fragments of the Red Planet here on Earth in the form of Martian meteorites.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: These are pieces of Mars that were blasted off the surface by asteroid strikes, and ended up being hurled towards the Earth.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Martian meteorites are extremely rare, but like all space rocks that fall to our planet, they become contaminated as soon as they get here, mixing with the air, dust, soil and water.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Scientists are so desperate to get their gloved hands on a direct sample from Mars and its moons because it would be pristine.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Dame Esther Rantzen died at her home in Bramshaw, in the New Forest, on 30 September A posthumous note written by Dame Esther Rantzen said she was "deprived of any choice over my own death".
sentences.article_title: Rantzen felt 'deprived of choice' over her own death

sentences.text: The farewell message was released as the 86-year-old broadcaster and campaigner's family confirmed she had been laid to rest in an "incredibly beautiful" private funeral last week.
sentences.article_title: Rantzen felt 'deprived of choice' over her own death

sentences.text: The Childline founder, who was diagnosed with stage four lung cancer in 2023, died at her Bramshaw home in the New Forest, Hampshire, on 30 September.
sentences.article_title: Rantzen felt 'deprived of choice' over her own death

sentences.text: A larger memorial service is expected to take place at a later date.
sentences.article_title: Rantzen felt 'deprived of choice' over her own death

sentences.text: Rantzen's daughter Rebecca Wilcox said the family had been inundated with messages since her death.
sentences.article_title: Rantzen felt 'deprived of choice' over her own death

sentences.text: "It's been hugely comforting to know that people around the world felt the same way about her as we did," she said.
sentences.article_title: Rantzen felt 'deprived of choice' over her own death

sentences.text: Dame Esther became a prominent campaigner for assisted dying in her later years, something MPs voted against legalising in September.
sentences.article_title: Rantzen felt 'deprived of choice' over her own death

sentences.text: In her note, she wrote: "It would have transformed the way I died if the law had allowed me to ask for assistance to die when my life had become unbearable.

sentences.text: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence Warning: this article contains discussion of eating disorders "If you keep this up, you'll be in a wheelchair at 30." That is what doctors told British long-distance runner Jake Smith four years ago.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: From the outside looking in, his career was flying.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: By the age of 23, he had signed a professional contract with Nike and represented Great Britain on the global stage.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: But at the same time, his body was deteriorating - enduring a relentless pattern of race, illness, injury, repeat.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Balancing an intense training regime with disordered eating meant the 28-year-old returned from a running camp in Uganda weighing just eight stone (51kg) at 5ft 5in (1.7m).
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: He had such brittle bones that he was told his career could be over.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: After suffering two stress fractures in the space of four months, Smith sought professional help and was diagnosed with REDs – relative energy deficiency in sport.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: It is a syndrome that can affect anyone and if left undiagnosed or untreated, can have an impact on performance and cause serious, long-lasting health problems.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: The symptoms are slightly better documented in women - just last month, tennis player Emma Navarro revealed her diagnosis and subsequent decision to step away from competition until 2027.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: But men are just as susceptible and due to stigma and lack of obvious warning signs, it can go undetected for longer and means many, like Smith, suffer in silence.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: BBC Sport explains what the condition is, how it affects men and women and why, despite its prevalence and severity, REDs remains a relatively under-reported and overlooked area of sports science.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: REDs can cause bone stress injuries, disrupted sleep, fatigue and low mood.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Left untreated, the condition can lead to serious long-term health problems, including osteoporosis, cardiovascular disease and fertility issues.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Dr Nicky Keay, an expert in hormone health, says many of these symptoms stem from hormonal disruption caused by insufficient energy intake.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "Hormones go to every single bit in your body.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: So, if your hormones are not working well for you, you're going to feel it in all sorts of different areas," she says.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "In order to have healthy hormones, they need to be fed regularly.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: If you're not doing that and there's an energy deficit, often some of those hormone systems will slow down or shut down completely." Women have a monthly barometer of their hormone health with the menstrual cycle, described by Keay as a "free monthly medical check".
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Put simply, she says, a woman suffering from REDs has her periods "switched off".
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: For men, it is more subtle – testosterone levels will drop, resulting in a reduced libido and fatigue.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: The impact on a woman's period is why the condition was first referred to in the early 1990s as the "female athlete triad".
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: But it was renamed by the International Olympic Committee in 2014 to acknowledge the broader range of symptoms of energy deficiency and that it also harms male athletes.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "We realised we were ignoring the other half of the population," Keay says.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "It's a strange situation because normally it's women's health that is the one being ignored but, in this situation, it's the men who weren't being recognised or represented." Twelve years later that decision appears to be vindicated, with recent research highlighting the prevalence in men.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Meta-analysis published in Australian journal Sports Medicine last year, following a study involving thousands of elite and amateur athletes around the world, indicated  44.2% of female athletes and 49.4% of male athletes had low energy availability.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Jake Smith was regularly getting injured So why is REDs so common?
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: One of the answers lies in the phrase 'lighter is faster'.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: For decades, it had been an accepted wisdom in sports like endurance running, cycling, climbing, horse riding, dancing and aesthetic sports like diving and gymnastics.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: And for athletes like Smith, it is how his problems started.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "I believed it for years.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: I thought that was the way forward," he says.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "I started thinking 'how do I improve my half marathon by 10 seconds?
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Is it a drop in weight?'.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: And that's when my head completely went." Initially, the strategy can work.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: When it comes to choosing energy to cover training demand or energy to stay healthy, the body has learned through evolution and threat of predators to always prioritise movement.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: It means that athletes can drop weight and still train and exercise and achieve good results.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: But eventually, the luck runs out.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Described by Keay as "fool's gold", the body will adjust to the energy deficit and cause a drop in performance and high risk of injuries.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: This video can not be played The athletes affected by relative energy deficiency in sport Olympic and world champion Jonny Brownlee acknowledges under-fuelling mistakes he made in his triathlon career contributed to serious injuries.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "I didn't see the importance of it.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Training came first and I think we weren't educated enough in how important fuelling was," he tells BBC Sport.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "You were seen, culturally, as a bit weak if you were fuelling on the bike.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: And the impact of that was definitely injuries - probably not recovering from my training quite as well as I should have done, stress responses, stress fractures.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: So there's that side of it and probably underperformance in races as well." Brownlee, who recently announced his retirement, believes the culture of not fuelling on the bike has now changed but a stigma lingers around REDs and the perception that it is a "female issue".
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "In females, there are more obvious signs but in males it can go under the radar a little bit and then it hits you by a really serious injury," he says.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "I think there's a stigma attached in there, or it's not looked at as the obvious answer to some of your problems, it's found later down the line.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Men also don't like to talk about under-fuelling because it's just seen as 'you probably should feel better and you should be on top of that'." It is those attitudes among male athletes that prompted Keay to conduct an experiment in 2019.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Assessing 50 male competitive cyclists, Keay found in her initial screenings that nearly half had poor bone health and 25% were suffering from REDs.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: The cyclists were then split into two groups and across a six-month period, one half continued their training and fuelling habits as before while the others were tutored by Keay and offered nutrition and training advice.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "The group that I left to their own devices unfortunately went on the default and they lost even more bone mineral density, similar to an astronaut in space… And they performed OK, but relative to their functional threshold power, they didn't get the race results that you would have expected.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "For the group I took under my wing, there was an improvement in their bone health and really good race results.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "So, I had evidence that REDs definitely does exist quite extensively in my group of the male cyclists and you're going to underperform if you don't fuel sufficiently.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: The good news is that REDs is reversible.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: But if you don't take action, it's a decline." Jonny Brownlee is a three-time Olympic medallist As the syndrome and its symptoms are still not commonly known, it is often difficult to know where to find help.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: After former GB runner Pippa Woolven's struggles with the condition, she set up a website called Project REDs which offers information and practical resources for athletes, coaches, parents and healthcare professionals.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Keay also helps people competing at all levels to recover from REDs.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Most of her patients are women, but she is starting to see more men reach out for help who, she says, are often in "bad shape".
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "I think the men are maybe more reluctant than the women, or maybe they don't realise they've got it.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Sometimes they might use a different word for it, they say burnout," Keay says.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "I don't mind that though because there is definitely a psychological aspect to REDs.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Why are you not eating the carbohydrates?" Sometimes, it's hard to answer those questions because the under-fuelling is unintentional, either from not understanding or underestimating energy requirements or failing to match an increase in the intensity or duration of exercise with higher calorie or carbohydrate intake.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: For others, former British cycling champion Brian Smith among them, the answer comes from intention.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "I always felt like I was overweight.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Everybody was under pressure regarding weight, but nobody really spoke about it," he says.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "I'm just under six foot and I've got large glutes and thigh muscles.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: As a road cyclist, I used to race at 68kg and for my height and build, that's quite skinny.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: I even got down to about 66kg and when I got down to that, I felt underpowered, I felt bad." Smith, now 59, only discovered he had been suffering from REDs during his career when he started running eight years ago and developed three severe stress fractures, including one in his femur.

sentences.text: The wreck remains surrounded by an exclusion zone in the Thames Estuary Three masts removed from a bomb-laden shipwreck in the Thames Estuary have been successfully taken to a maritime museum.

sentences.text: The poles, delicately removed from the SS Richard Montgomery in September, will be kept at the Historic Dockyard Chatham.
sentences.article_title: Masts from explosives-packed ship taken to museum

sentences.text: The masts had been visible from the Essex and Kent coasts since the doomed vessel sank with 1,400 tonnes of explosives onboard in 1944.
sentences.article_title: Masts from explosives-packed ship taken to museum

sentences.text: Junior transport minister, Kier Mather said removing the masts had reduced the risk of them toppling on to and detonating the bombs.
sentences.article_title: Masts from explosives-packed ship taken to museum

sentences.text: "As the vessel has aged, the masts continued to place significant load on the structure," he said in a written statement to Parliament.

sentences.text: "Their removal has reduced that risk and supports the long-term safe management of the site." A deadly secret in the Thames - what is the SS Richard Montgomery?

sentences.article_title: Masts from explosives-packed ship taken to museum

sentences.text: A crane supported the poles as they were sliced off and lifted to safety.
sentences.article_title: Masts from explosives-packed ship taken to museum

sentences.text: Tommy Robinson, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, arrives at Southwark Crown Court for his five-day trial Political activist Tommy Robinson used "bully-boy, intimidatory tactics" to frighten two Daily Mail journalists, forcing them to employ security or leave home, a court has heard.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: The 43-year-old from Bedfordshire, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, is charged with two counts of harassment causing fear of violence towards reporters Andrew Young and Jacob Dirnhuber.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: Opening the trial, prosecutor Ben Holt said the case was about Yaxley-Lennon's reaction to what he perceived to be "an unnecessary intrusion into his holiday" in the aftermath of the 2024 Southport attacks.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: Robinson, who founded the English Defence League, entered not guilty pleas to the charges in July last year.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: Holt said Dirnhuber had to move house because of the alleged harassment, while Young was given a close protection officer by the Daily Mail after photographs of his wife and children were posted on Robinson's X account.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: Robinson posted on X before the trial began to thank the social media platform's owner Elon Musk for funding his case – and said his court fees to date had cost him £400,000.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: The trial at Southwark Crown Court concerns Yaxley-Lennon's response to articles published by the Daily Mail and MailOnline Holt said that after the murders of three young girls in Southport on 29 July 2024, Yaxley-Lennon made a number of posts on social media.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: This alerted the Daily Mail and Mail Online to the fact that he was in Cyprus.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: The Daily Mail published articles that included photographs of the defendant, including one showing him "reclining on a sunbed using his mobile telephone".
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: Southwark Crown Court heard that over the following days, he made a series of posts on his X account in response.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: On 4 August, these included: "The daily mail have purposely gave the location of where I am with my children knowing full well that people want to kill me." Another post said: "The daily mail have purposely doxed the exact location of my family.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: How can they be allowed to do this'." There were no identifiable pictures of Yaxley-Lennon's children published by the Daily Mail or in the Mail Online, jurors were told.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: Holt said the trial was about Yaxley-Lennon's reaction to the articles, and accused him of using "bully-boy tactics" to "intimidate" the journalists.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: "He chose to frighten them, arrange for individuals to go to their addresses," said the prosecuting counsel.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: "On social media — to millions of followers — he circulated images of their homes.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: "His supporters got involved — threatening the journalists.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: "Understandably, you might agree, they were scared; in some circumstances, being forced to leave their homes." Stephen Yaxley-Lennon spoke to crowds outside Southwark Crown Court before heading inside The court heard that on 5 August, Dirnhuber received a number of direct messages from Robinson/Yaxley-Lennon.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: These included "you have endangered my children", "I'll be knocking at your door," and "let your bosses know I'm coming to all of your houses".
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: The jury panel also heard details of an alleged phone conversation between Yaxley-Lennon and Young.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: "He said that he had Mr Young's telephone number.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: He recited his home address," Mr Holt told jurors.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: Yaxley-Lennon then became, according to Mr Young, "increasingly menacing".
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: The prosecutor continued: "He raised his voice, he was swearing and shouting.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: "He said that he had been researching Mr Young's family and threatened to publish photographs of them and their addresses online.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: "Mr Lennon told Mr Young that he would be coming to Mr Young's house and he would have to move house.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: "He was going to shove a camera in his face and ask questions.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: "Mr Young told him that he did not want to engage with him — all complaints should be directed to the Daily Mail legal department.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: "Mr Young believes Mr Lennon said 'I'm coming to get you'." The prosecutor said it would have been "inevitable" that Robinson's posts would lead his supporters to "pick up the baton" and target the journalists.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: He referred to a post from somebody who had displayed a picture of Mr Young's Suffolk address online.
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: The jury was told that Yaxley-Lennon's case was that his family "had been put in danger by the actions of the Daily Mail" and he had acted to "protect his family".
sentences.article_title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters

sentences.text: On X he posted: "What is good for the goose is good for the gander." The trial, in front of a jury of nine men and three women, is expected to last for five days.
