sentences.text: Chancellor John Healey is planning to increase taxes on the bank sector, senior banking executives have told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Healey has described banks as part of "the crown jewels" of the UK economy, but leaders in the sector have said it will be "on the menu" at the Budget in two weeks' time.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: The biggest four banks collectively made about £15bn profit in the first six months of this year, and trade unions have called for them to face additional taxes.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: The trade body for the banking sector, UK Finance, warned "further increases in bank taxes would weaken competitiveness, discourage investment and job creation, and work against the government's ambition to deliver growth in every postcode".
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Shares in banks including Lloyds and NatWest fell on Friday on expectations that the sector would be hit by tax hikes.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: The firms were among the biggest fallers on the UK stock market, with both dropping more than 2%.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Barclays fell only slightly and HSBC actually rose as both have large international businesses and would be less affected by a hike in UK taxes.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: What is the Budget and what could be in it?
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: There are a number of ways the chancellor could extract more money from the sector.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: One option is for Healey is to reverse a reduction in the surcharge that banks pay on corporation tax, from 8% to 3%, introduced in 2023, by Conservative chancellor Jeremy Hunt.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Critics argue this would be unfair noting the cut coincided with a rise in corporation tax from 19% to 25%.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Healey could also raise the bank levy - a small percentage charged on loans.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: The BBC understands that the Treasury is leaning towards changing the surcharge if they were to go ahead as it is easier to change an existing tax rather than impose a new windfall tax.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Reversing the 2023 surcharge rate would raise around £2bn.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: However, the last government was persuaded that adding 8% on top of corporation tax of 25% would leave UK banks struggling to compete with European and US rivals - so it may be that it is raised, but not all the way back to the 8% level.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Speaking to the press in Bangkok, Healey praised the role banks play in the British economy.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Sir Philip Augar, an author and former banker in the City of London, told the BBC's Today programme there was "room for a moderate increase" in taxes on the sector that could raise up to £3bn a year.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: He said lenders were enjoying "booming conditions", benefiting from higher interest rates which boost their profits.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Rising interest rates have expanded the margin between the rate at which banks lend to customers and the rate they pay savers.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Sir Philip added that when the banking sector "hits really rocky times it expects the taxpayer to bail them out - when it hits boom times, it expects some kind of special treatment".
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: He said banks cannot simultaneously be "too big to fail and too big to tax".
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Paul Nowak, general secretary of the Trades Union Congress, which represents trade unions, said Britain's four biggest banks are making a billion pounds a week, with bonuses at post-financial crash records.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: "These are bumper profits - driven by high interest rates and households' mortgage misery," he said.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: "Now it's time to make sure banks pay their fair share," he added.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: "But if the chancellor does ask the Banks to pay a fairer share of tax in the Budget, that's 100% the right call," he added.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: There is another option that has been discussed with Treasury officials.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Currently banks can use losses from the past to offset against profits - thereby reducing their tax bill in any given year.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Lloyds in particular has been a beneficiary of this policy, as large losses from the financial crisis have been used to lower tax bills ever since.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Some analysts and bank executives have pushed the idea of a moratorium on this practice for a few years, which would yield an estimated extra £1bn per year for the Treasury.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: That would provide a windfall while being "a lot more bearable", in the words of one bank executive.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: It would also spare foreign banks from an additional hit, including JP Morgan, whose chief executive Jamie Dimon has warned that the UK already has one of the highest tax burdens on banks in the world.

sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: However, industry leaders say any form of tax rise that hits UK banks and exempts foreign banks' operations in the UK would be hard to square with the government's push to back British business.

sentences.text: The operators of Newby Island landfill have been ordered to take action over odours Milpitas, an affluent city in California's Silicon Valley tech hub, has an odour problem.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: For decades, residents have had to endure rank smells wafting from industrial sites, among them a 342-acre landfill.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "When I first moved here, I could not open my window for over 10 years," says Chia-Ling Kong, an engineer for a tech firm who lives around half a mile from the dump.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: While things have got better in recent years, Kong says she and her neighbours must still contend with around "two or three hours of bad smells a day".
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Perhaps befitting Silicon Valley, the community is putting its hopes in technology.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: The operators of Newby Island landfill have been ordered by local authorities to use drones and install monitors to systematically track and measure the chemicals responsible for bad odours.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: They have also been told to automate the collection of landfill gases responsible for smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Kong is optimistic a data-driven approach will make a difference.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Hopefully with this continuous monitoring, it makes it easier to pinpoint problems at the moment it starts." The operators of the landfill say they are committed to operating it safely and protecting air quality.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Just like in Milpitas, where Kong is part of a citizen's campaign against the odours, communities around the world are raising a stink about bad smells making day-to-day life miserable.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Sometimes a rubbish dump is to blame, or it might be a sewage treatment works, or a reeking factory.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: When the complaints start stacking up, resolving them is not always simple.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Many countries have no regulations in place dictating how to manage smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: In the US, for example, the Environmental Protection Agency does not regulate environmental odours as a pollutant.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This leaves states and local governments to take charge of the issue.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Urban sprawl is often part of the problem, bringing communities closer to stinky facilities that may historically have been kept at a distance.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This is creating more demand for technologies to monitor and prevent smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Odour consultant Micheal Bull says people are increasingly concerned about neighbourhood stinks.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "You're getting developments being built nearer to odorous processes… as land has become more valuable, there is also infilling," Bull says.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: He is speaking about his experiences in the UK, but it's a similar story in many parts of the world.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Bad smells from waste sites are among the most difficult to resolve The technologies used to tackle industrial pongs generally fall into three categories: they absorb odours; convert them into something less smelly through a chemical reaction; or burn them away.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Experts on fixing industrial odours say that the best technologies, when used correctly, can remove 90% or more of the target compounds responsible for smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: But this can be expensive and some operators opt for simpler and cheaper solutions.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: These include masking odours from landfill or sewage processing by spraying giant quantities of deodorisers.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Odour experts contacted for this article were dubious about the effectiveness of such industrial scale air fresheners.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "In my view they're not likely to change the odours," says Bull, who likens them to fabric conditioner.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Bad smells from waste sites – a common cause of complaints – are among the stinkiest and most difficult to resolve, according to Carlos Diaz, an environmental consultant based in Spain.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Landfill is difficult to treat because you have a very large surface," he says.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: In some places at least, technology is making a real difference.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Residents in Des Moines, Iowa, have long complained of the so-called Eastside Funk, a putrid scent that residents report drifts over parts of the city.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: A study commissioned by city authorities showed that a trio of industrial meat companies were among culprits.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Within 10 miles, there's about half a million people," says Dalton Jacobus, who works in the Department of Neighborhood Services.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "If the winds are out of the wrong direction, 100,000 people can be in the middle of that odour plume." The authorities are now paying around $240,000 (£182,000) a year on technology to track the stink, so they can take action.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "What we wanted to do was build a ring of odour monitors around the facilities that we suspected of emitting odours," says Jacobus.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: The monitors, which measure levels of chemical compounds in the air, work in combination with a weather station to provide real-time data on the concentrations that are coming from each facility based off the wind patterns.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This has put an end to finger pointing about who's to blame each time a smell sparks complaints, says Jacobus.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Smithfield Foods, which operates a meat processing in Des Moines, says it has invested $2m to install a regenerative thermal oxidiser that destroys the chemicals associated with bad smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Even so, the company says it does not believe it is the source of odour complaints.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Before installing the monitors – which some local companies help pay for – officials in Des Moines would drive out to the source of a complaint to sniff the air.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Relying on the human nose to sniff out industrial smells is still commonplace.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Claudia Barrios Obregón from Kunak, the company behind the monitors in Des Moines, says: "Right now, the way that cities control or measure odours is olfactometry: a human panel measures and gives an opinion of what the odour is like.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: But that's not that realistic." The Spanish company's monitors are an example of so-called electronic noses that make it easier to detect smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Whatever technology is used, it can be hard to keep everyone happy, as smells are so subjective.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Unfortunately, the general rule is that the nastier we perceive the odour to be, the more sensitive towards it we are," says Johan Lundström, a professor in the science of smell at the Karolinska Institute in Stockholm, Sweden.

sentences.text: Alan Feeney has stepped down as deputy mayor of Solihull, and given up his role as a councillor in both Solihull and Birmingham Warning: This report contains racist and offensive language.

sentences.article_title: Reform councillor quits over offensive remarks

sentences.text: The Liberal Democrats don't tend to go for rhetorical fireworks or verbal kneecappings when grumbling about their leader.

sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: In the last week, two members of Sir Ed Davey's frontbench have resigned because they were unhappy with him, the party's direction and how policy is decided.

sentences.text: It meant the prospect of a lengthy and potentially testy meeting for Sir Ed with his MPs on Tuesday evening.

sentences.text: The Liberal Democrat leader arrived smiling, flanked by several loyal MPs, but made no comment as he entered the room.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: Nearly four hours later, when the meeting broke up, his deputy Daisy Cooper said: "There is overwhelming support for Ed in the parliamentary party and a real sense that we need to come together as a group." Earlier, behind closed doors, we understand Sir Ed told his MPs: "We have made changes.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: I am happy to embrace more changes.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: I want us to work as a united front." Another tacit nod to things being less than united recently.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: In recent months he has appointed a new chief of staff, Ruth Younger, and James Holt, a veteran of the party's years in coalition government, as political director.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: Last week's resignations were described to the BBC by one party figure as a rather Lib Dem insurrection – dissent expressed modestly.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: Neither Charlie Maynard, a former Treasury spokesman and Alison Bennett, a former care and carers spokeswoman, have been publicly explicit about the reasons for their departures and both sought to express their concerns to Sir Ed privately and discreetly.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: And, it is understood, there was no coordination between them in the timing of their resignations.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: They were departures that led to fury among some of their colleagues, irritated that it made the party look divided.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: The resignations were the most clear indicators yet of an anxiety that has been bubbling away for over a year among some Liberal Democrat MPs.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: The essence of that anxiety is a fear they are not making enough of an impression and impact for the 72 MPs they have in parliament.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: "The big frustration is the lack of cut through, being noticed.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: We are the biggest third party in the Commons in a century.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: But parliament doesn't shape things as much as it used to.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: It's about algorithms now," is how one figure put it.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: They added: "In the world of social media there is an incentive, even a financial incentive, to be divisive and extreme.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: That's a sandpit we refuse to play in." Nonetheless, the party is planning to up its social media game, but do so in line with what it sees as its authentic temperament and values.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: Those around Sir Ed Davey privately acknowledge there is what they claim to be a "small group" of Lib Dem MPs who are not happy with his leadership.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: It is suggested that number isn't greater than "half a dozen" - a phrase used by several people we have spoken to.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: But the anxiety about a perceived lack of impact involves far more MPs than that.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: Some previous private critics have been won over by the recent changes to Sir Ed's team and are pleased to see the government talk about issues they care about: the European Union, changing the voting system for Westminster elections and social care in England, for instance.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: They also hope the scale of their local campaigning, rather than poor national opinion poll ratings, will be more significant come the next general election.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: "But we're getting there putting in place the structures to better deal with that and keep MPs happy." "Why would we get rid of our leader when no one else is pitching to be our leader?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: We need to let Ed get on with it," said another MP.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change

sentences.text: But they all know the underlying concern about impact – the challenge of being noticed – is real and not going away.

sentences.text: Around 650 more prisoners in England and Wales are due to be released under the second tranche of the government's early release scheme.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Under the scheme, eligible prisoners are released after serving a third of their total custodial sentence rather than after 40% or 50% of the term.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: People sentenced for manslaughter, rape, serious child sex and grooming offences are excluded.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: This is not the first time a government - Conservative or Labour - has released prisoners early to make space in England and Wales' overcrowded prisons.

sentences.text: BBC Verify has looked at the reasons why ministers say this latest scheme is necessary.

sentences.text: The prison population in England and Wales on 12 October was 87,033, which was 97.8% of useable capacity , external .
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) has previously warned the prison population will overtake capacity as soon as this November.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: In the long-term the MoJ has projected that the capacity of all prisons will rise to around 99,000 by 2032 as a result of more prisons being built by this government.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: But it also projected that the prisoner population would rise to about 104,000 by 2032 if the Sentencing Act 2026 - which provides for earlier release - did not come into force.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: An AI tool may be able to help doctors judge how ill a patient is using a single photograph of their face, say US researchers.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: Trained on millions of healthy faces, and 35,000 photos of cancer patients, the tool can make estimates on survival by looking closely at features near the eyes, the scientists say.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: While it's a long way from being suitable for use in hospitals, the researchers say their goal is to help doctors recommend the right treatments for their patients.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: The preliminary findings are published in the Lancet Digital Health , external journal.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: The researchers developed two AI tools to estimate biological age and predict cancer survival from a single face photo.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: The face on the left shows features most important to cancer survival outcomes, while the right face shows those key to age.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: Areas shown in yellow had the greatest impact on predictions.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: The 'FaceSurvival' AI tool suggests the area under the eyes and around the bridge of the nose are the most vital parts of the face to assess when estimating how long they might have left to live.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: These metrics applied across many different types of cancers, varying in severity, including ones that had spread to the patient's bones or brain.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: Most of the cancer patients, who were from the US and the Netherlands, were in their 50s or 60s, but some were children, while others were in their 90s.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: Doctors already examine patients and run comprehensive checks and tests to judge how unwell they are, and what their prognosis might be.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: The AI tool, which has a patent application pending, is designed to help doctors doing this work, not replace them.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: Lead researcher Dr Raymond Mak, from Mass General Brigham in Boston, explained: "As the population ages, physicians need better ways to estimate physical reserve and frailty before recommending intensive treatments such as radiation, surgery or systemic therapy.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: "Our goal is to make face photograph-based health assessment more quantitative, consistent and scalable so it can support personalised treatment decisions rather than replace physician judgment." Collagen: Do you drink it?

sentences.text: More than 24,000 Covid vaccine-harm claims have been made - most relating to the AstraZeneca jab The government has committed to reform of the scheme that provides financial support for those injured or bereaved by vaccines.

sentences.text: It was a key recommendation of the UK Covid Inquiry, and has been a focus for campaigners.
sentences.article_title: Covid vaccine compensation scheme set for overhaul after Inquiry criticism

sentences.text: One campaign group has welcomed the recognition that vaccine injury and bereavement is real and that the current scheme is not fit for purpose.
sentences.article_title: Covid vaccine compensation scheme set for overhaul after Inquiry criticism

sentences.text: But it says it wants a clear commitment to action by ministers, rather than simply saying they will look further at what needs to be done.
sentences.article_title: Covid vaccine compensation scheme set for overhaul after Inquiry criticism

sentences.text: The benefits of vaccination are well documented.
sentences.article_title: Covid vaccine compensation scheme set for overhaul after Inquiry criticism

sentences.text: The AstraZeneca Covid jab is credited with saving millions of lives worldwide.
sentences.article_title: Covid vaccine compensation scheme set for overhaul after Inquiry criticism

sentences.text: But some people have experienced harm.
sentences.article_title: Covid vaccine compensation scheme set for overhaul after Inquiry criticism

sentences.text: In her fourth report, the chair of the Covid Inquiry, Baroness Hallett, called for better support for those affected.
sentences.article_title: Covid vaccine compensation scheme set for overhaul after Inquiry criticism

sentences.text: She said while this was a minority, the way they are supported needed urgent reform.
sentences.article_title: Covid vaccine compensation scheme set for overhaul after Inquiry criticism

sentences.text: More than 24,000 people have made Covid-related claims to the Vaccine Damage Payment Scheme (VDPS), a form of financial support paid by the government, but just over 1% have resulted in one-off tax-free awards of £120,000.
sentences.article_title: Covid vaccine compensation scheme set for overhaul after Inquiry criticism

sentences.text: The report called for "urgent" reform of the scheme, saying that it is "not sufficiently supportive".
sentences.article_title: Covid vaccine compensation scheme set for overhaul after Inquiry criticism

sentences.text: It said the current system, in which those affected must show they have been at least "60% disabled", does not work effectively for Covid vaccines.
sentences.article_title: Covid vaccine compensation scheme set for overhaul after Inquiry criticism

sentences.text: In its response to the report, the government says , external it is committed to reviewing the scheme to ensure it is "fit for purpose and delivered effectively." Ministers in England have promised to work closely with the other nations of the UK as well as those injured by the Covid vaccine and their families.
sentences.article_title: Covid vaccine compensation scheme set for overhaul after Inquiry criticism

sentences.text: One of the main campaign groups for those who were injured by the Covid vaccine is Vaccine Injured and Bereaved UK.
sentences.article_title: Covid vaccine compensation scheme set for overhaul after Inquiry criticism

sentences.text: The group welcomed the government's acknowledgement that vaccine injury and bereavement were real and that the VDPS is not fit for purpose.
sentences.article_title: Covid vaccine compensation scheme set for overhaul after Inquiry criticism

sentences.text: But in a statement it said that was not the same as committing to action.
sentences.article_title: Covid vaccine compensation scheme set for overhaul after Inquiry criticism

sentences.text: "After more than five years of campaigning, and with the Covid-19 Inquiry explicitly calling for reform as soon as possible, we had hoped the Government would finally come forward with a clear commitment to action, not simply say it would look further at what needs to be done.
sentences.article_title: Covid vaccine compensation scheme set for overhaul after Inquiry criticism

sentences.text: "We understand that work may be needed to develop the reforms, but there is a real difference between saying you will look at something and committing to deliver it.
sentences.article_title: Covid vaccine compensation scheme set for overhaul after Inquiry criticism

sentences.text: "Today, we have no clear timetable, no certainty about what will change and no assurance about when families will finally see meaningful progress." The Government response also said it recognised there were concerns about the running costs of the scheme.
sentences.article_title: Covid vaccine compensation scheme set for overhaul after Inquiry criticism

sentences.text: Last month it was revealed that the VDPS has cost £83m to run since April 2022 .

sentences.text: This video can not be played Same-day test helps detect hidden infections in critically ill children A pioneering same-day test has been used to detect hidden and drug-resistant infections among children in intensive care.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Respiratory samples from more than 100 critically ill young patients at London's Great Ormond Street Hospital (GOSH) were sent for what is known as metagenomic testing. , external It can identify bacteria, viruses and fungi from a single sample, which in many cases influences what doctors prescribe.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Metagenomics can detect infections that standard tests miss, meaning better outcomes for some critically ill patients.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: In March, 10-year-old Willow Crowther became dangerously ill with pneumonia, which triggered a seizure and multiple cardiac arrests.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Willow, from Kent, was admitted to intensive care at GOSH.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Her mum, Stacey Moore, was told she had a 50% chance of survival.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: "The consultant said... we should bring our family up to say goodbye to her.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: This is how critical and in how much danger she was of passing away." The team at GOSH used metagenomics - a diagnostic test that works by sequencing all genetic material present, in contrast to conventional methods where clinicians need to decide in advance what they're looking for.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: The test identified that Willow had a drug-resistant bacterial infection which needed a different antibiotic to the one she had been prescribed.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: The test helped doctors identify which antibiotic would be effective in treating Willow "The fact that they had a test there available to her was paramount.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: It saved her life," said Stacey.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: "It's a miracle she's here and we're extremely grateful for that," added Willow's dad, Russ.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: With the right treatment, Willow was eventually able to recover from her infection, but needed several months in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: She is one of many patients at the children's hospital to benefit from the new type of testing.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: During a study in 2024-5 metagenomic testing was used on 122 critically ill children in the paediatric intensive care unit (ICU) at GOSH.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: The results have now been published in the Lancet Microbe.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Metagenomic testing analyses all genetic material in a sample and can detect thousands of different pathogens.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: By contrast, the most common method of identifying bacteria is by trying to culture them in Petri dishes, a technology that has been used since Victorian times.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Another test, PCR, can identify viruses and some bacteria, but doctors need to specify what they are trying to detect.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Metagenomics testing at GOSH was able to identify around nine in 10 bacteria and viruses and all fungi in samples.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Willow celebrated her 10th birthday in August In a quarter of cases, the results influenced prescribing decisions, including starting, stopping or changing an antibiotic.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Dr Sam Ray, consultant in paediatric intensive care medicine at GOSH and co-author of the study said traditional testing required clinicians to make an educated guess about which infection they were looking for.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: "The study has helped us to spot infections we would have missed, get children on the right treatment and stop antibiotics when we know they aren't going to work.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: "Removing unnecessary treatment is incredibly important for the fight against growing antimicrobial resistance." Metagenomic testing at GOSH also detected 50 organisms not identified by routine diagnostics, meaning it could play an early warning role against new infections.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Dr Julianne Brown, head of the GOSH Metagenomics Service and co-senior author of the study said the new testing was being gradually rolled out to around 30 intensive care units across the UK treating both adults and children.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: "It could be a powerful tool for identifying new infections that pose a pandemic threat," she added.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Trans patients should be cared for on single-sex hospital wards or bays that align with their biological sex rather than their gender identity, according to new NHS England (NHSE) guidance.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: It says when this is not "clinically appropriate" then alternative arrangements should be made and the dignity and safety of all patients should be maintained.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The guidance also says staff facilities should be used by people based on their biological sex, while trusts should ensure enough alternatives to single-sex facilities, such as single-occupancy toilets, are offered.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: Previous NHSE guidance suggested patients and staff could be accommodated on wards or use facilities based on their gender identity.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: That meant that a trans woman – a biological male who identifies as a woman – could have chosen to be on a women's ward, or a trans man – a biological female who identifies as a man – could have opted for a men's ward.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: That guidance was withdrawn following the Supreme Court ruling in April 2025 that under equality law the term "sex" means biological sex and "woman" refers to a biological woman.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The judgment said for a space or service to be single sex it should only allow those of the same biological sex to use it.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: Also under the new guidance issued on Thursday, NHSE emphasised that in order to avoid discriminating against trans people they should be offered gender neutral spaces.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: But the guidance also says decisions may have to be made on a case-by-case basis and must ensure clinical needs are met.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: It also makes clear that there are circumstances where clinical need is the overriding priority, including on emergency units and urgent care settings.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: In addition to the patient document of the guidance, NHSE has published advice for trusts on how to organise changing rooms, toilets and other single-sex facilities for staff.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: Again, it says they should be used by people based on their biological sex, not their gender identity.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The document encourages NHS trusts in England to carry out an audit to ensure they are offering enough alternatives to single-sex facilities, for instance, gender neutral or single occupancy toilets.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: Pressures on hospitals mean many have already struggled to keep wards single sex.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: NHSE data shows that the number of breaches of the previous mixed-sex accommodation guidance has been growing every year since 2021- where members of the opposite sex were placed on a single-sex ward.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The most recent figure for August 2026 shows there were 5,520 breaches, compared to 3,853 in June 2025.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: Sex-based rights charity Sex Matters has welcomed the guidance as a "momentous shift back to reality", but is concerned about how it will be applied.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: "NHS patient data is a mess, with potentially thousands of trans-identifying people recorded as the opposite sex," CEO Maya Forstater said.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: Trans rights organisations TransActual and Trans+ Solidarity Alliance have said they are concerned NHS staff will be unclear on how to safely look after trans patients.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: "This guidance will not survive contact with reality in resource-strapped hospitals and will create unworkable operational challenges," they said.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The NHS has been at the centre of a number of high-profile arguments over the interpretation of equality law and workplace regulations.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: In January 2026, Darlington Memorial Hospital was found to have violated the dignity of a group of nurses who complained about a transgender colleague - a biological male who identified as a woman - being allowed to use the female changing rooms.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The nurses were told they should change somewhere else if they objected.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The tribunal concluded that the trust had indirectly discriminated against them.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The nurses are currently seeking £400,000 from the NHS to cover their legal costs.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: One of the nurses who brought the action, Bethany Hutchison, who is now president of the Darlington Nurses Union, says they welcome the "clear and necessary guidance" from NHSE, but the test will be whether trusts follow it.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: "The Darlington nurses should never have had to take their own employer to court to secure privacy, dignity and lawful single-sex facilities," she said.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: "Enforcement cannot continue to depend on the courage and personal sacrifice of individual nurses." In Scotland, another employment tribunal found, in December 2025, that a nurse, Sandie Peggie, had been harassed by NHS Fife over its interpretation of rules on single sex spaces.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: Peggie had complained about a doctor, who was a trans woman, using the female changing rooms.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: She was suspended after raising concerns.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The tribunal dismissed her other claims of discrimination and victimisation.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: An appeal is under way and expected to reach the courts next year.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: Louis, Otis and Ben all have differing opinions on whether teens should use protein powder Twelve-year-old Ben is desperate to try protein powder but there's one hurdle: me, his mum.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: "I've asked about 20 times and you just keep saying no!", he says, claiming it would make him "fitter and bigger" and that his male friends use it.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: In recent years, there's been an explosion of products marketed as "high protein", including milk, yoghurt, breads, cereals, bars and powders.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Social media is flooded with adverts for various supplements, including protein powder.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: As a health journalist, I'm sceptical and think at Ben's age he must be getting enough protein through his diet.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: So, do experts think it's safe for pre-teens and teenagers or is a big, juicy steak just as good?
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: In recent years, there has been an explosion of products marketed as "high protein"... ... however, protein is found in lots of everyday foods, including meat, fish, eggs, dairy, bread, grains and pulses My sport-obsessed son, who already eats a healthy balanced diet, asks me about protein powder on a regular basis.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: His friend Louis, 12, has been using protein powder once or twice a week for nearly a year, after a workout and on top of whole foods.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: His parents are aware of this.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: "I think it's helped, it gives me more energy and it's helped me grow, probably," he says.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: But Ben's other friend Otis, who is 13, is not keen on the idea and feels there is pressure on young people to take protein supplements.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: "They might just start using them without thinking about the consequences or what effects it may have on them." Proteins break down into amino acids that help the body grow and repair.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: But your body can't make all the amino acids it needs on its own, so you need to get more - known as essential amino acids - through your diet.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: For an adult with a healthy weight, the recommended daily amount of protein you should be eating is 0.75 grams per kg of body weight, according to the NHS.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: A good rule of thumb is that the amount of protein you have for each meal should fit into the palm of your hand.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: If you exercise a lot, and when you get older, you need more protein so you could have up to 2 grams per kg of body weight.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: But do teens really need it if they're eating well?
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: This video can not be played Do you really need protein powder to build muscle?
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: For teenage boys and girls "you can get all the protein that you need from food alone", says registered dietitian Nichola Ludlam-Raine.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: It is important that teenage girls, especially, get enough iron and calcium, so Ludlam-Raine says not to become overly focused on protein at the expense of other nutrients.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Protein shakes, powders or bars can be useful for some, including high-level athletes and those who have certain allergies, but they should not replace a healthy diet.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: There can also be some unwanted side effects from using protein powders such as bloating, gas, cramps, and diarrhoea.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Those with pre-existing health conditions should not use it unless they have been told they can by their doctor.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Ludlam-Raine points out that the protein powder market is not as tightly regulated as medicines.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: "Of course, you can get reputable companies who do third-party testing and make sure that what you see on the label is what is in the inside, but that's not always the case," she says.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: "And ultimately you can't just have a shake and your biceps grow." Some protein powders contain high amounts of added sugar, artificial ingredients, and hidden stimulants.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Dr Ramnik Mathur is a consultant paediatrician from West London.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: He explains that we need micronutrients like zinc, calcium and magnesium, which are found in whole foods.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: So, if meals are replaced with protein shakes, those nutrients are lost.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Experts suggest spreading out protein across the day and aiming for 20-25g per meal.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: If you're keen to up your intake, try some of these recipes.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: During puberty when children have growth spurts, they do need more protein because their body is growing rapidly, building new muscle and bone mass.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: But Mathur says there are risks to eating too much protein.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: "If you look at social media, they'll say you need to eat a lot of protein, but your body can handle only so much." He explains that if you eat too much, it has to be excreted by the kidneys and liver which can become overloaded and have serious health implications.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: The key takeaway from Mathur: "If a 12-year-old child is eating a healthy balanced diet then they shouldn't need any more protein." Ludlam-Raine's advice is to get teens to improve their diet first before taking any protein powder, especially regularly.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: If they still want to use it, speak to a registered dietitian or nutritionist first.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Now off I go to tell my son the answer is still no - and the experts say the same.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: The amount of time children in England spend on screens at school could be harming their "physical and developmental health", a group of more than 150 clinicians has warned.

sentences.text: GPs, paediatricians and other specialists said in an open letter to Education Secretary Lucy Powell and Health Secretary Yvette Cooper that tablets and laptops are being used without a full understanding of their long-term health impacts, including on eye health.

sentences.text: South Cumbria support group Menopause Matters is inviting people from across the county to share their experiences A support group is holding a county-wide event for women coping with pain associated with menopause and perimenopause.
sentences.article_title: Online event offers support for menopause and pain

sentences.text: South Cumbria support group Menopause Matters is holding an online forum for World Menopause Day, inviting people to share their experiences and ask questions.
sentences.article_title: Online event offers support for menopause and pain

sentences.text: World Menopause Day is an annual event started by the International Menopause Society (IMS), with this year's theme Chronic Pain At Midlife.
sentences.article_title: Online event offers support for menopause and pain

sentences.text: Facilitator Leigh Williams said she hoped Sunday's free online event, being held between 19:00 and 20:00 BST, would "open up the conversation" around pain and menopause.
sentences.article_title: Online event offers support for menopause and pain

sentences.text: Menopause Matters also holds a monthly cafe-style drop-in in Barrow-in-Furness, offering women the opportunity to meet up in an informal environment.
sentences.article_title: Online event offers support for menopause and pain

sentences.text: Williams was inspired to become a facilitator because of her own experience with perimenopause and chronic pain.
sentences.article_title: Online event offers support for menopause and pain

sentences.text: "I know what it feels like when pain starts to shrink your world," she said.
sentences.article_title: Online event offers support for menopause and pain

sentences.text: Participants will include a GP, pelvic health physiotherapist, local authority health professional, support group facilitators and people with lived experience of persistent pain.
sentences.article_title: Online event offers support for menopause and pain

sentences.text: "What we've seen through the menopause cafe is that women's experiences don't fit neatly into boxes," Williams said.
sentences.article_title: Online event offers support for menopause and pain

sentences.text: "We might start with menopause and very quickly find ourselves talking about pain, sleep, mental health, stress or neurodiversity.
sentences.article_title: Online event offers support for menopause and pain

sentences.text: "No one person on this call has all the answers.
sentences.article_title: Online event offers support for menopause and pain

sentences.text: Some of the common symptoms of perimenopause and menopause , external are painful, similar to musculoskeletal pain or symptoms of ﬁbromyalgia.
sentences.article_title: Online event offers support for menopause and pain

sentences.text: They can include muscle and joint aches, stiffness and swelling, reduced strength and pins and needles.
sentences.article_title: Online event offers support for menopause and pain

sentences.text: "Menopause is something that effects 50% of the population, so we absolutely should be expecting a level of health," Williams added.
sentences.article_title: Online event offers support for menopause and pain

sentences.text: "Some women can be experiencing these symptoms for a decade - that's a long time to be uncomfortable.
sentences.article_title: Online event offers support for menopause and pain

sentences.text: "Health and wellbeing isn't just the absence of ill-health, it's about being able to thrive and that's what I'm striving for." Anyone wishing to take part in the free online conversation can do so by reserving a space on the event's booking website , external .
sentences.article_title: Online event offers support for menopause and pain

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down We know some people love a cuppa, even when it's sweltering, and that actually makes scientific sense.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down, says Dr Daly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Research suggests your body sweats more quickly to get rid of the excess heat after a hot drink.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Your body is trying to keep your core temperature steady at about 37 degrees celsius.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So hot tea won't necessarily help you cool down more quickly - the key thing is to stay hydrated no matter the temperature of the liquid.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You don't need to shun your favourite coffee either just because it's hot - although too much caffeine can make the body produce more urine, and leave you dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: For matcha fans, the drink contains more caffeine than a cup of tea but less than a regular coffee.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Dr Daly says one or two coffees a day should make little difference to your hydration levels - but five or six will start to have an effect.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Bear in mind that drinking alcohol also dehydrates.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You could structure your day differently too, and take a southern European approach to eating.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Have an early breakfast, an afternoon siesta while it's very hot and then a late dinner.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Ofcom is investigating whether Meta breached its duties under the UK's online safety laws with the launch of its "Instants" feature on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: The tool - allowing users to take and share an instant image with close friends, that disappears once viewed - was launched on Meta's photo-sharing app in May as "a new way to share photos in the moment".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But the regulator said the social media giant had not properly assessed risks posed by the feature prior to launching it - something it is required to do under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA).
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said in a statement that it "takes its regulatory obligations under the Online Safety Act seriously".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," they said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation." Ofcom said its probe would examine whether Meta breached OSA duties by not carrying out "a suitable and sufficient illegal content risk assessment and children's risk assessment before the launch of Instants".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Under the UK's sweeping online safety rules, platforms including Meta must carry out and update risk assessments to comply with a range of duties, including to tackle illegal content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: They must also show how they prevent children permitted to use their services from encountering content deemed harmful for them.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: This spans material relating to pornography, or promoting self-harm or suicide - as "priority primary content" - alongside things like abusive, hateful or bullying content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Our online safety laws are clear – significant changes to platforms must be risk assessed before they're launched," said Ofcom enforcement director George Lusty.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "This is a vital step that tech firms must take to protect their users," he added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Images shared with Instants can be viewed by those who have been selected as "close friends" by a user, or those who they follow and are followed back by.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta says the feature has a range of built-in protections, including for younger users with Teen Accounts, including preventing screenshots, reshares or forwarding of Instants.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But disappearing messages and images have been singled out previously as posing particular risks for child or teen users of some apps .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Safety by design must be built in, not bolted on, and today's investigation shows we'll take action where we have concerns that providers are failing to comply," Lusty added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: All three companies have appeared in court this week, arguing they should not need to provide so much information in response to Ofcom's formal requests.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta has separately also argued Ofcom should not be able to levy fines for breaches based on its global annual revenue.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: It also contends that its messaging and image-sharing apps should not have to face additional requirements under the OSA, such as tackling paid-for fraud ads.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature
