sentences.text: A second head teachers' union has called for a halt to graded Ofsted inspections in England, saying it is "increasingly concerned about the welfare and morale" of its members.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: The Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL) also raised the prospect of potential strike action, saying a new grading system had become an "overbearing mess".
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: On Friday, Ofsted's chief inspector Sir Martyn Oliver said an independent survey of education providers showed it was "on the right track" with inspections.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: The Department for Education (DfE) said ministers were "working with Ofsted and school leaders to ensure accountability is fair, proportionate and focused on helping every school get better".
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: ASCL's announcement comes after another union, the National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT) , said changes Ofsted made to inspections just under a year ago had been severely harmful to school leaders' welfare.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: ASCL said it had passed a motion of no confidence in "the ability of Ofsted's leadership to address the damage being done by the new inspection system", adding that it was "increasingly concerned about the welfare and morale of members".
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary, said the union did not take the step "lightly", but added Ofsted's "warm words about recognising wellbeing pressures... have not been matched by the action necessary" and that "negotiation [had] hit a brick wall".
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: "The current system is not fit for purpose.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: It is an overbearing mess and urgently needs to be reviewed," he said.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: Why the shake-up of school inspections risks causing new problems What is Ofsted and how does the new school ratings system work?
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: ASCL called on the government to pause inspections and review the system, and said it would survey members on whether to hold an informal ballot on industrial action if there was no change.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: In response, Ofsted said it had "worked hard to reduce the pressure of inspection in recent years, but we know workload and wellbeing remain a challenge".
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: "We are working with the Department for Education on this and we will keep listening to feedback from professionals as we continue to improve what we do," a spokesperson added.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: England's schools inspectorate introduced the report card system to replace its previous one or two-word judgements last November, following the death of head teacher Ruth Perry, who took her own life after Ofsted downgraded her school from "outstanding" to "inadequate".
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: An inquest ruled that an Ofsted inspection had contributed to her death in January 2023.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: That led to a change in how Ofsted assessed schools, bringing in report cards designed to grade schools on several areas, rather than focusing on one overall grade.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: An example of a new Ofsted inspection report Last month, the NAHT said testimonies from its members, seen by the BBC, suggested some school leaders had faced "intolerable" pressure because of the new inspections, leaving them "overwhelmed" and "anxious".
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: It warned the system could pose a "risk to life" if changes were not forthcoming.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: An independent report, commissioned by Ofsted to evaluate its new framework, concluded this week that leaders were "generally positive" about their inspection experience, and that it was "more collaborative and accounts for context better than previous inspections".
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: But it also said nearly half (48%) of school leaders who responded to its survey said their staff's mental wellbeing had been negatively affected "a fair amount" or "a lot" by a recent inspection.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: The interim report was based on focus groups and nearly 700 responses from school, college and early years leaders who were invited to complete a survey following inspections this year.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: A full report is due to be published next year.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: Sir Martyn said: "The data published today shows that we are on the right track.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: "I know that workload and wellbeing in education continue to be challenging, and I don't take that lightly.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: York was the subject of the city-wide pilot, which also put on workshops for parents and offered special training for early years staff.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Twenty local authorities across England are now signed up to launch similar schemes to tackle the number of pupils starting school without being fully toilet-trained.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: The government said the pilot's results were "encouraging", and confirmed they were committed to 75% of pupils reaching a good level of development at the end of their first year in school by 2028.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Since April this year, parents across York have been targeted via GP surgeries, pharmacies, family hubs, schools, nurseries and libraries with information and offers of support on how to potty-train their child ahead of starting school.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Potty training guides were sent out to all families across York who had a child starting reception in September - with the aim that all children could use the toilet independently by the time they started school, except those with medical issues or special educational needs.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: The results from all 55 mainstream primary schools across the city, shared exclusively with BBC News, suggested there had been a 43% drop since last year in the number of children who were not fully toilet-trained when they started school.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Across York last September, 148 out of 1,364 reception pupils (11%) were recorded as not being toilet-trained when they started school.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: This year, that fell to 85 reception pupils out of 1,374 (6%).
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Parents Natalie and Lucy, who both have daughters starting reception next year, have welcomed the extra support on offer.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Mum Natalie says there's a lot of conflicting pressures on parents about the right time to potty-train Lucy said she had noticed the drop-in sessions on potty training in her local children's centre and thought it was a "really good idea".
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "I think it's really important that children are more prepared for that aspect of starting school," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Natalie said getting her daughter Freya potty-trained in time for school has been a priority, but feels there is a lot of pressure on parents to do so.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "I think going to school is hard enough for children," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "When I was little, we still had the terry towelling nappies and they had to be washed and hung on the line.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: So I think with disposable nappies it's easier," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Around one in four children started school in England and Wales last year not fully toilet-trained, and teachers said they have been spending over an hour a day changing nappies, according to the latest research from the children's charity Kindred Squared , external .
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Felicity Gillespie, chief executive of Kindred Squared, told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that children not being potty trained when starting school was "a real concern for teachers".
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "They tell us that they're losing, on average across the country, a day a week of teaching time to dealing with potty-training issues." Gillespie is keen to spread the message that "it's best for children to be coming out of nappies" when they are between 18 and 30 months old.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "When the teacher's leaving the class to change someone's nappy, the rest of the class is having their learning broken up.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: So everybody loses out,” she added.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: The ability to listen to and follow instructions is another skill that helps pupils get the most out of learning when they start reception class Jo Mould, who teaches reception at Robert Wilkinson Primary Academy in York, said she has noticed an improvement in pupils being ready for school this year.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "We've spent more time teaching in these last three weeks than we have in previous years," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "The children have come in so ready to learn, because they're more settled and regulated socially and emotionally.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: We've had a really, really positive start to the school year." Jo Mould says not having to deal with toilet training has meant more time spent teaching her pupils York councillor Bob Webb said the impact of the scheme had been "so positive" for both schools and families.

sentences.text: Sir Anthony Seldon, former head teacher and author on AI in education, says the technology is being used more and more frequently, but that its introduction has been "chaotic and anarchic".

sentences.text: The government says its changes to the curriculum in England will give children digital skills and help them spot disinformation.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: England's biggest school leaders' union has called for a halt to graded Ofsted inspections, saying they could pose a "risk to life" for school staff.

sentences.text: The National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT) said the change to inspections, rolled out nationally just under a year ago, had been severely harmful to school leaders' welfare.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: It said schools should instead be rated using short narrative reports that set out their strengths and areas they could improve.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Ofsted said it had worked closely with unions and parents to develop the new report card inspection system and that it would continue to grade schools.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Ofsted, England's schools inspectorate, introduced the report card system to replace its previous one or two-word judgements last November, following the death of head teacher Ruth Perry , who took her own life after Ofsted downgraded her school from "outstanding" to "inadequate".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: An inquest ruled that an Ofsted inspection had contributed to her death in January 2023.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: That led to a change in how Ofsted assessed schools, bringing in report cards designed to grade schools on several areas, rather than focusing on one overall grade.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: An example of a new Ofsted inspection report But the new system has faced criticism since it was first proposed , with Perry's sister Prof Julia Waters saying it appeared to be "a rehash of the discredited and dangerous system it is meant to replace".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The NAHT issued a claim in the High Court for a judicial review over the changes, arguing there had not been adequate consultation on the new report cards before they were introduced, but this was rejected.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Nearly a year after it was fully rolled out, the NAHT said evidence from its members suggested the new system is having a detrimental impact on school leaders' mental health.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies this week

sentences.text: The Orionids are fast and bright, entering our atmosphere with speeds of around 41 miles per second.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies this week

sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies this week

sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies this week

sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies this week

sentences.text: Experts warn children as young as five years old are now being groomed on social media and gaming sites Experts are urging parents to talk to their children amid warnings social media grooming is becoming "quicker" and "easier" than ever before.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Childline said Snapchat, TikTok and Instagram were the top platforms children named in counselling about online sexual abuse last year.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: The companies have been approached for comment.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Avon and Somerset Police's child exploitation prevention officer Andri Nicolau said children as young as five can be targeted through social media, gaming and messaging platforms.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: She urged parents to encourage kids to ask for help without fear of blame or punishment.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: The warning comes after three men were jailed for grooming a 17-year-old girl on Snapchat before raping her.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Research by the NSPCC found sexual communication offences involving children in the South West have more than doubled since the offence was introduced seven years ago, to 756 in 2024/25.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Of those, 300 were recorded by Avon and Somerset Police, 96 by Gloucestershire Constabulary and 61 by Wiltshire Police.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: The charity also said Snapchat was mentioned in 324 counselling sessions about online sexual abuse between April 2025 and March 2026, a 19% increase on the previous year.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: TikTok (234) and Instagram (197) were the next most frequently mentioned platforms.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Chris Sherwood, chief executive of the NSPCC, said: "It's deeply disturbing that hundreds of children have come to us in the past year alone, disclosing experiences of online sexual abuse linked to these popular apps and platforms.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Aqeel used social media, including Snapchat, to arrange to meet young girls.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: He also filmed some of his offences and threatened to share intimate videos and images.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: New data suggests that this particular form of exploitation of children, known as 'sextortion', has also reached record levels.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: The Internet Watch Foundation (IWF) said there has been a sharp rise in the number of young people contacting its confidential Report Remove helpline , external because they fear sexual images of themselves have been shared, or could be shared, online.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Criminals try to extort or blackmail their victims by threatening to publish the images, which have often been taken by the child themselves.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Nicolau said children spending more time online meant they were increasingly vulnerable to grooming, which is "easier" and "quicker" than ever before.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "With online gaming and social media, you have kids from five years old online, some of them have their own phones, so it can be any age," she said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: She works with schools to inform children how to be safe online, but said they are often unaware of the risks, including not viewing people they meet online as strangers and expecting them to be "nasty" from the start.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Nicolau encouraged any child or young person who believes they are being groomed to "find someone they are comfortable with and speak to them".
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: She said the police might not be the first choice, but speaking to somebody they trust is what mattered.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Nicolau urged parents to talk to their children and not take away devices or ban them from platforms, warning this could make them feel they were to blame.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Sit down with your child, tell them it's not their fault, even if they've sent indecent images of themselves," she said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Often, particularly if it's to do with grooming or any kind of sexual or romantic relationship, children can be really scared of being judged and embarrassed to talk," said Bradshaw.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Perpetrators are always adapting ways they can better reach young people, whether that's through gaming or social media," he said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: He said another worrying trend was young people turning to AI rather than adults for advice and support about online harms.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Ella Bradshaw from the NSPCC said children don't speak out because of fear of judgment Ellen Roome, from Cheltenham, who has been campaigning for improvements to online safety since the death of her son Jools in 2022, said not enough is being done to protect young people on social media.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Children are regularly being fed content that is either violent or grooming material and I think as it stands, there isn't any platform that is fully safe for them," she said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "I do think that the social media ban for children will help, but they need to make sure that it is enforced and social media companies are held to account." Ellen Roome has secured rights for families to get social media data from their children's accounts after they pass away.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Simmons-Read said the social media ban for under 16s , which is due to come into force in 2027, "doesn't go far enough", could be bypassed by criminals and could even discourage young people from speaking up about online grooming.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "We want tech platforms to invest more in detecting exploitation when it's happening on their platforms," he said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: A government spokesperson said it was preparing legislation to make it impossible for children to take, share or view nude images on their devices, which would make the UK the first country to do so.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Alongside this, tech companies must be part of the solution and meet their legal and moral obligations.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Where they fall short, the government will not hesitate to step in," the spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Kerry Smith, chief executive of the IWF, said: "We welcome the commitment to introducing nudity blocking technology on children's devices – but there really is no time to lose." Meta, which owns Instagram and Facebook, said it is working to "fight and prevent grooming in a range of ways".
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said: "This includes restricting contact between adults and teens they're not connected to, and using technology to find and remove known child exploitation imagery.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "We also use behavioural signals to identify accounts showing possible signs of grooming or a sexual interest in children.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Based on the strength of the signals, we either prevent them from finding and following teens or we remove their account completely." Snapchat and TikTok have all been approached by the BBC for comment.

sentences.text: "Courage and leadership" are needed to ensure Northern Ireland catches up on tackling climate change.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: The new chair of the Climate Change Committee, Nigel Topping, is spending two days on a fact-finding mission to hear the thoughts of people across different sectors.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: He said Northern Ireland was a small nation that could be "agile and innovative" in tackling challenges like increasing renewable energy, improving waste management and reducing emissions.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: But he warned that a failure to act would mean missing out on innovation opportunities, paying more for energy and damaging the health of children.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: The Climate Change Committee is an independent body advising the UK and devolved governments on emissions targets.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: Over the course of a two-day visit, Topping is meeting farmers, people from the business sector and politicians.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: It is being described as a fact-finding mission, looking at "challenges and opportunities".
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: He acknowledged that politics in Northern Ireland was "complex" and that "when things flip-flop, it doesn't help", due to the impact on investment decisions and people's choices.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: But he said there was "a real sense of collectively wanting to catch up" and avoid anyone being left behind on the road to net zero.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: "You've had these lags where there's been no ministers sitting and so there hasn't been policy - there's been civil servants working but no policies," he said.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: Topping said people were experiencing climate change firsthand, with the effects of extreme weather being felt around the UK.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: And he added that that would continue, until emissions reached net zero.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: "But I see this as a race between our kind of obstinate, greedy selves and our brilliant, innovative selves," he said.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: "And all of us have a bit of both of those extremes and we have those as societies, and I think if we can really tap into backing ourselves as innovators, then we can take this as an opportunity.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: "The most important thing for me is that we're going to do this and we're going to have to do this because this is a collective chance for humanity.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: "So we can either see it as a burden and complain all of our way and be laggards, or we can see it as an opportunity and say, we're resilient, we're adaptive, we're innovative.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: Nigel Topping is the new chair of the Climate Change Committee When asked what will be the consequences of not taking that "opportunity", he is blunt.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: "There's two ways of answering that question.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: One would be, oh, if Northern Ireland doesn't do anything, it doesn't make much difference to the world," he said.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: "The other would be, if Northern Ireland doesn't do anything, it misses out on all the innovation opportunities, because other people take those.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: "It continues to poison its children's lungs because it doesn't fix the air quality, and it continues to pay more for energy than it needs to.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: "So that's like, dumb, dumb, dumb - why would you do that?
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: "So don't get stuck in the we're only small, what difference do we make?
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: The Orionids are particularly fast and can leave trails in the sky that last a few seconds after the meteor itself has gone.

sentences.text: The display occurs at around the same time each year when the Earth passes through a trail of dust and debris left behind by Halley's Comet.

sentences.text: The Orionids are particularly fast, entering the atmosphere at around 41 miles per second.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: As tiny particles from Halley's comet enter the Earth's atmosphere they heat up and produce streaks of light across the night sky that we see as meteors.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: Halley's Comet is one of the most famous comets in our Solar System and has been observed from Earth for centuries.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: It takes around 76 years to complete one orbit of the Sun and was last seen from Earth in 1986.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: Halley's Comet is not expected to be visible from Earth again until 2061, but its debris will continue to produce meteor showers each year.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: In fact, the Earth encounters material left behind by it twice a year, resulting in the Eta Aquariid meteor shower in May and the Orionids in October.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: The meteors appear to radiate from the constellation of Orion, which is where the shower gets its name, but they can appear anywhere across the night sky.

sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: Bird migration is a visible annual event at Castle Espie Avian flu, cost-cutting and Brexit are among the reasons behind the transfer of captive birds from one of Northern Ireland's best-known wildlife sites, according to the charity that runs it.

sentences.text: Brazil's government says deforestation rates in the country's Amazon and savanna regions have fallen to record lows ahead of a presidential election run-off in which the rainforest's future is a key issue.
sentences.article_title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms

sentences.text: Left-wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, when he assumed office three years ago, pledged to end deforestation by 2030 in the Amazon.
sentences.article_title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms

sentences.text: It had surged under his right-wing predecessor, Jair Bolsonaro.
sentences.article_title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms

sentences.text: Lula will face Bolsonaro's son Flavio in the run-off on 25 October, with polls suggesting a neck-and-neck race.
sentences.article_title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms

sentences.text: Flavio is expected to continue his father's policies if he wins, though he has pledged to fight organised crime in the Amazon.
sentences.article_title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms

sentences.text: Satellite data shows that in the year to July 2026, the deforestation rate fell by 41.8% in the Amazon - the biggest drop since records began in 1988.
sentences.article_title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms

sentences.text: The fall in the Cerrado, Brazil's savanna region, was 23.8%.
sentences.article_title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms

sentences.text: The Amazon rainforest - the world's largest - is a crucial buffer in the global fight against climate change and 60% of it is located in Brazil.
sentences.article_title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms

sentences.article_title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms

sentences.text: During Bolsonaro's presidency from 2019 to 2022, the Amazon lost nearly 60% more in forest lands compared to the previous four years, news agency AFP reported, citing official data.
sentences.article_title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms

sentences.text: Lula reversed his policies and oversaw deforestation rates drop to a six-year low during his first year in office.
sentences.article_title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms

sentences.text: Lula tightened up environmental monitoring and penalties for illegal logging.
sentences.article_title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms

sentences.text: "Our goal is to achieve zero illegal deforestation by 2030," he said in a post on X on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms

sentences.text: Tropical rainforests like the Amazon are home to millions of species.
sentences.article_title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms

sentences.article_title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms

sentences.text: But they have come under increasing pressure from decades of deliberate land clearance for agriculture and logging, as well as climate change, which scientists warn can create conditions for wildfires.
sentences.article_title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms

sentences.text: Brazil's Environment Minister Joao Paulo Capobianco described the decline in Amazon deforestation as "absolutely stratospheric".
sentences.article_title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms

sentences.text: It was an "historic achievement" for Brazil, said Marcio Astrini, executive secretary at climate advocacy group Observatorio do Clima.
sentences.article_title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms

sentences.text: It showed that "with political will, it is possible to curb deforestation and greenhouse gas emissions", Astrini said.

sentences.text: Eight capybaras are the first litter since just one pup at the park four years ago Curraghs Wildlife Park has experienced its busiest October weekend ever after the birth of eight capybara pups, which staff say have "delighted" people and boosted conservation funding.

sentences.text: Democratic Party Senator Jeanne Shaheen has spearheaded the cross-party statement from several US senators A bipartisan group of US senators has signed a letter demanding an urgent investigation into disruptions to SpaceX's Starlink internet network in Ukraine.

sentences.text: Starlink is a vital tool allowing Kyiv to guide drones to Russian targets and protect its own skies, but on Tuesday night Ukraine said it had unexpectedly restricted how fast drones could fly while maintaining internet connection.
sentences.article_title: US senators call for investigation into Ukraine's Starlink restrictions

sentences.text: In the letter, sent to the US defence department inspector general, the senators express "grave concern" about reports of speed curbs between 12 and 14 October.
sentences.article_title: US senators call for investigation into Ukraine's Starlink restrictions

sentences.text: Asked whether the US might have had a role in the slowdown, a US official told the BBC "no such request was ever made by the president [Donald Trump]".

sentences.text: The letter, led by Jeanne Shaheen - a Democrat on the Senate's Foreign Relations Committee -  calls for the inspector general to find out whether the restrictions were caused by the US defence department or its contractors.

sentences.text: It says "restrictions reportedly degraded Ukraine's ability to conduct defensive operations against Russian drone and missile attacks on civilian infrastructure".
sentences.article_title: US senators call for investigation into Ukraine's Starlink restrictions

sentences.text: Starlink, which is owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX, restricted speed limits on Tuesday night to 100mph (160km/h), meaning any weapons that travelled faster than that lost connectivity to the network.
sentences.article_title: US senators call for investigation into Ukraine's Starlink restrictions

sentences.text: Conservationists say Jersey is an "important refuge" for red squirrels With growing concerns that red squirrels could soon become extinct in England , one Channel Island is a corner of the British Isles where they maintain a stronghold.
sentences.article_title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving

sentences.text: Jersey is home to a thriving red squirrel population, thanks to the complete absence of grey squirrels, which carry a virus deadly to their red cousins.
sentences.article_title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving

sentences.text: Red squirrels are endangered in the UK , with about 120,000 to 160,000 left in the wild and various projects are aiming to boost those numbers.
sentences.article_title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving

sentences.text: There have some strongholds in England , external , particularly islands, and 75% of the British population is in Scotland , external .
sentences.article_title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving

sentences.text: However, despite not being native to Jersey, Henry Glynn, an ecologist with the National Trust of Jersey, said they "really are iconic for Jersey".
sentences.article_title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving

sentences.text: He said: "When you speak to people who have come over to visit the island from the UK, a lot of them will say that one of the things they want to do whilst here is to see a red squirrel, because they're so rare and so difficult to see in large parts of the UK.
sentences.article_title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving

sentences.text: "That is actually really special for them." Red squirrels are not native to Jersey, having been introduced in 1885.
sentences.article_title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving

sentences.text: However, Glynn described them as "naturalised", having become "assimilated into the natural environment" over many years.
sentences.article_title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving

sentences.text: The animals have previously featured in Visit Jersey , external tourism campaigns, including one fronted by conservationist Ben Fogle.
sentences.article_title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving

sentences.text: National Trust ecologist Henry Glynn says red squirrel sightings can be a highlight for visitors The National Trust of Jersey said the island wa s an "important refuge" for the red squirrel, where they were " fairly widespread , external ".
sentences.article_title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving

sentences.text: It said the inland valleys and woodlands were the best places to spot them.
sentences.article_title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving

sentences.text: The species is legally protected, which means it would be a criminal offence to harm them.
sentences.article_title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving

sentences.text: Nina Powell, senior animal carer at the JSPCA [Jersey Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals], said Jersey has a "good population" of squirrels and that "you can see them almost anywhere".
sentences.article_title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving

sentences.text: While the primary reason for their success is the lack of grey squirrels, Powell said they also thrived "because people look out for them".
sentences.article_title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving

sentences.text: She said: "A lot of people do support them, put out feeders and stuff like that.
sentences.article_title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving

sentences.text: "Their habitats are decreasing everywhere... but we do have quite a lot of nature reserves.
sentences.article_title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving

sentences.text: "In some places, we've got rope bridges which really help them cross the roads, and our speed limits are quite low, so that helps them as well".
sentences.article_title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving

sentences.article_title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving

sentences.text: She said: "We want to keep all animals as wild as possible, so we try and be as hands-off as possible.
sentences.article_title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving

sentences.text: "Some of them don't like us... some of them are quite sweet.
sentences.article_title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving

sentences.text: They really do vary in personality." Glynn agreed that their success had come in part because of the efforts of islanders.
sentences.article_title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving

sentences.text: He said: "They're really beloved amongst the local community as well.
sentences.article_title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving

sentences.text: A lot of people put out squirrel feeders or love to see them in the garden.
sentences.article_title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving

sentences.text: It marks a successful first year for a major community-led effort to restore one of the capital's rarest native wildflowers, vital for bees, butterflies and rare moths.
sentences.article_title: Volunteers help save one of London's rarest plants

sentences.text: Led by Citizen Zoo and Habitats & Heritage, the tower mustard project brings together a network of land managers, community groups, conservation partners and volunteers.
sentences.article_title: Volunteers help save one of London's rarest plants

sentences.text: The plants, grown by volunteers, are being reestablished at sites across London, in regions where tower mustard was previously known to occur.
sentences.article_title: Volunteers help save one of London's rarest plants

sentences.text: At the core of the project are the Mighty Mustard volunteers.
sentences.article_title: Volunteers help save one of London's rarest plants

sentences.text: In March, they attended a workshop, learned how to sow the tiny seeds, and were given their own growing equipment, including pots, seed trays and soil.
sentences.article_title: Volunteers help save one of London's rarest plants

sentences.text: Seeds were sourced from London's last remaining tower mustard populations in Lesnes Abbey Woods in Bexley and Stain Hill Reservoir in Richmond-upon-Thames.
sentences.article_title: Volunteers help save one of London's rarest plants

sentences.text: Charlotte Harris, nature conservation manager at Habitats & Heritage, said: "[We] are passionate about engaging people in conservation initiatives.
sentences.article_title: Volunteers help save one of London's rarest plants

sentences.text: Through this tower mustard project, we have enjoyed giving local residents the unique opportunity to get hands-on in conserving one of London's rarest plants.
sentences.article_title: Volunteers help save one of London's rarest plants

sentences.text: "We've found the volunteers have become really attached to [them]." Seeds have now been planted at Wimbledon Common, Hounslow Heath, Lesnes Abbey Woods and Barnes Common.
sentences.article_title: Volunteers help save one of London's rarest plants

sentences.text: Harris added: "We are hoping that this model can be used as a blueprint for helping other rare plants with volunteer input in the same way." The final planting day is at Hampton Court Palace's Home Park on Tuesday, where plants raised separately by the Historic Royal Palaces Gardens Team and volunteers will be used.
sentences.article_title: Volunteers help save one of London's rarest plants

sentences.text: Botanist Dr Mark Spencer has also provided expert support throughout the project.
sentences.article_title: Volunteers help save one of London's rarest plants

sentences.text: Prior to the project, the once widespread plant was only found in two locations in the capital Tower mustard, or Turritis glabra, is a native UK herb that has suffered steep decline due to habitat destruction and changes in land management.
sentences.article_title: Volunteers help save one of London's rarest plants

sentences.text: It is thought to survive at around 30 sites across England.
sentences.article_title: Volunteers help save one of London's rarest plants

sentences.text: The species is assessed as near threatened on the Great Britain Red List and endangered in England.
sentences.article_title: Volunteers help save one of London's rarest plants

sentences.text: Growing to around one metre tall and producing delicate white flowers, tower mustard is associated with open and disturbed habitats and supports pollinators.
sentences.article_title: Volunteers help save one of London's rarest plants

sentences.text: This community-led model builds on Citizen Zoo's successful Hop of Hope project which saw volunteers rear large marsh grasshoppers from eggs at home, going on to release the species in wetlands across Norfolk.
sentences.article_title: Volunteers help save one of London's rarest plants

sentences.text: Elliot Newton, director of rewilding at Citizen Zoo, said the company hopes to roll out more projects to preserve plants in the face of climate change.
sentences.article_title: Volunteers help save one of London's rarest plants

sentences.text: "In London alone, we've lost 185 species of plant.
sentences.article_title: Volunteers help save one of London's rarest plants

sentences.text: They have gone extinct in recent history." He said Citizen Zoo have many other plants on their radar, including copse bindweed, a native British climbing plant.
sentences.article_title: Volunteers help save one of London's rarest plants

sentences.text: The tower mustard project is funded by the Greater London Authority's Green Roots Fund and Thames Water.
sentences.article_title: Volunteers help save one of London's rarest plants

sentences.text: The project brings together Habitats & Heritage, Barnes Common, Lesnes Abbey Woods, Wimbledon Common, London Borough of Hounslow, London Borough of Richmond upon Thames and  Historic Royal Palaces.
sentences.article_title: Volunteers help save one of London's rarest plants

sentences.text: The Exmoor Dark Skies festival celebrates its 10th anniversary in 2026 Stargazers and astronomers are preparing to enjoy a festival that celebrates the beauty of the night sky.
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: The annual Exmoor Dark Skies Festival is being held from 16 October to 1 November and this year is its 10th anniversary.
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: Taking in villages and towns surrounding Exmoor National Park, the event offers walks, talks and shows - putting the dark, clear, night sky into full focus.
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: Granted by the International Astronomical Union in 2011, the status aims to safeguard the right of any citizen to enjoy the night sky by helping to limit light pollution.
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: Photographers and astronomers can enjoy clear views of the stars during the festival Colman said there is "very little light pollution on Exmoor", adding it "enables the dark to be really dark with none of the pollution impacting".
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: "In the core of the reserve, there's an area where there is no light at all in a huge area - and that just makes the sky so much clearer and you're able to see some incredible constellations.
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: "You can see the Milky Way - it really is fantastic." Photographs taken during previous dark skies events show incredibly clear views of the stars against a clear, dark backdrop.
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: Locations such as Wimbleball Lake are big draws The National Park said it designed the event in 2017 to, in part, help local businesses towards the end of the traditional tourism season.
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: In Dunster, on the edge of Exmoor, the Yarn Market Hotel manager Antony Brunt said in recent years, "it has become much more widely known - and now we literally have people ringing us up to book".
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: The hotel hosts special trips during the festival, led by a local astronomer, and runs visits to various sites and events across the park.
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: Brunt said the festival brings in people from all over the UK, adding: "It's getting to a quieter time of year and these people, they really enjoy coming down.
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: "We have a group that come each year, in fact, twice a year.
sentences.article_title: What is behind the success of dark skies festival?

sentences.text: For people to come regularly twice a year to the same hotel, they must be enjoying the stargazing part of the weekend." The growing popularity of the festival meant that many events sold out before the opening day.

sentences.text: Marine ecology dog Sgiath at work A working dog from the Scottish Highlands has been named animal of the year by a charity for hunting down an invasive marine creature called the carpet sea squirt.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: This organism, also nicknamed "sea vomit", is particularly harmful to coastal wildlife and economies.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Working at low tide with her owner, Dr Texa Sim, black Labrador Sgiath has found hundreds of colonies of the sea squirt, which - if left uncontrolled - can smother and kill native species.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Sgiath (pronounced Skee-ah) is thought to be the UK's first sea squirt-hunting dog.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Carpet sea squirt can be tricky to spot among seaweed "She's a natural," says Sim proudly.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: The International Fund for Animal Welfare (IFAW) , external is awarding Sgiath animal of the years at its 26th annual animal Action Awards ceremony on Thursday 15 October.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Sim, a marine ecologist based near Glencoe, has had Sgiath since she was a puppy and the bond between the two is strong.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: "Sgiath is incredibly clever.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Her problem solving and her ability to take on new challenges and learn so quickly are just phenomenal, and it's so amazing to watch." As a pup, Sgiath was trained as a mountain rescue dog.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: The Labrador proved to be so good that Sim wondered if she could use her skills to help with marine conservation work.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Sgiath has been trained to recognise the scent of the carpet sea squirt.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: And now, the six year old joins her owner on the beaches to sniff it out.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Sim says the dog is always right when pointing out a sea squirt, which can be difficult to spot, looking like slime among seaweed and on structures like pontoons and oyster cages.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Carpet sea squirt, or sea vomit, has spread to several places around the UK "When I first started this project, I genuinely didn't know whether it would work," said Sim.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: "No one had really explored whether dogs could help tackle this problem in the marine environment.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: It began as a proof-of-concept project and has exceeded every expectation I had." Dogs' scent detection skills are often used in conservation work on land, including tracking endangered species and helping investigate environmental crime.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: At low tide, Sgiath can, as Sim puts it "dive down under the seaweed".
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: "She just does a survey with her nose, essentially, she can pinpoint exactly where it is, so it's much easier," she said.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Marine experts believe that carpet sea squirt, formally named Didemnum vexillum, came from Japan.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: It arrived on the shores of the south of England and Wales in 2008.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: It can appear in various shades - from orange to cream -  and has now spread to several seaside locations across the UK.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: It reproduces quickly during the warmer summer months and, with warming seas, there are fears it could spread further.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Dr Martyn Kurr, a marine biologist from Bangor University told BBC News that non-native or "biofouling" species, like the carpet sea squirt, can outcompete native wildlife for valuable nutrients.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: "These species also clog up aquaculture pens, marine infrastructure, and machinery such as boat propellors," he explained.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Efforts to control and clean up these problematic marine invaders costs millions of pounds every year across Europe.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Sgiath is also a trained mountain rescue dog To get Sgiarth proficient in both mountain rescue and marine conservation has needed hard work and long hours from both dog and owner.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: To locate and draw attention to a lost hiker on mountainous terrain, Sgiath is trained to bark and bounce around.

sentences.text: But it was his ambitious proposal to bring together regional rivals India and China, alongside Nepal, to tackle these shared threats that drew particular attention.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: Shah called for the creation of a Himalayan Climate Resilience Mechanism to strengthen cross-border disaster response and the sharing of scientific data and expertise in one of the world's most environmentally fragile and geopolitically sensitive regions.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: "Let the Himalayas become a laboratory of international co-operation rather than a frontier of fragmented information," he said.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: A senior official at Nepal's foreign ministry, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the proposal was still at an early stage.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: "The PM's proposal has given a political direction.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: Our ministry is working with other relevant agencies to put forward a preliminary framework which can be the basis for building common understanding," the official said.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: Neither India nor China has formally responded to the proposal.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: The BBC has contacted their foreign ministries for comment.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: But can Nepal really bring the two regional giants together to confront a shared climate threat in a region where they have long been locked in bitter territorial disputes?
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: India and China share a disputed frontier stretching roughly 3,500km (2,175 miles), much of it across the Himalayas.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: Their competing territorial claims have led to a war, deadly clashes and repeated military stand-offs along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), the de facto boundary separating areas under their control.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: But the mountains that have long been a source of friction between the two countries are also facing an urgent climate threat.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: Temperatures in the Himalayan region are rising faster than the global average, accelerating glacier retreat and permafrost thaw and contributing to growing risks of landslides, rockfalls, avalanches and glacial lake outburst floods.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: Such disasters can sweep across national boundaries, threatening lives, infrastructure and livelihoods far downstream - making co-operation between the countries sharing the Himalayas increasingly important.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: Further east, on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, glaciers have shrunk by 24% in area over the past six decades, Kang Shichang, director of the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Institute of Mountain Hazards and Environment, told China's People's Daily Online.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: Experts say the retreat of glaciers can cause glacial lakes to expand, increasing the risk of sudden, potentially devastating floods that can cross borders into countries such as Nepal, India and Bhutan.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: Several major rivers flowing through these countries originate on the Tibetan Plateau.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: The plateau now has more than 14,000 glacial lakes, covering over 1,100 sq km, according to People's Daily.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: And the dangers extend beyond flooding.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: A 2024 study published by the American Geophysical Union projected a significant rise in landslide hazards across the Himalayas and Tibet in the coming decades due to increased rainstorms.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: While the largest absolute increases are expected in already vulnerable areas, including India's Garhwal and Kumaon regions and Nepal, the greatest relative increase is projected on the Tibetan Plateau.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: The growing risks make co-operation more urgent.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: But past efforts by India and China to work together on Himalayan environmental issues have made little progress.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: The two Asian powers have often found common ground at UN climate negotiations, pushing back against Western demands for emissions cuts and arguing that developing countries should not bear the same burden as industrialised nations.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: Yet they have no dedicated agreement to jointly address the impacts of climate change in the Himalayas.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: In 2009, India and China agreed to undertake joint research into the impact of global warming on glaciers in the Himalayas and Tibet.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: Following a visit to Beijing, India's then environment minister Jairam Ramesh announced that the Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology and China's Cold and Arid Regions Environmental and Engineering Research Institute would collaborate on the project.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: Hundreds of people were killed in the deadly flood that tore through the China-Nepal border in August But the initiative went nowhere, according to a scientist involved in the effort.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: "One meeting was held between us and the Chinese side and that was it, nothing came out of it," said Dr DP Dobhal, a retired glaciologist who headed the glaciology programme at the Wadia Institute.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: "What happened after that no one knows," he added.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: Since the early 2000s, India and China had agreements under which Beijing provided flood-season hydrological data on the Brahmaputra and Sutlej, two major rivers originating in Tibet.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: But in August 2025, India's junior foreign minister Kirti Vardhan Singh told parliament that both agreements had expired.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: China had stopped sharing data on the Brahmaputra in June 2023, while India had received no data on the Sutlej since 2022.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: China has not publicly explained the latest interruption.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: But when it withheld similar information in 2017, amid a tense military stand-off with India, Beijing blamed technical problems at its hydrological monitoring stations in Tibet, Singh said.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: Some analysts see a glimmer of hope in the recent thaw between India and China, marked by high-level political engagement and moves to revive cross-border trade through Himalayan routes.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: "These developments suggest there might be more room for the three countries to explore climate-related co-operation," says William Yang, senior analyst for North East Asia at the International Crisis Group.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: But he says Beijing is likely to remain cautious about any major agreement with India and Nepal, as border disputes remain unresolved.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: One major obstacle is that information vital for understanding climate risks can also have military value.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: Experts have raised concerns over climate-related risks as the Himalayan snow cover melts rapidly Such tensions have also hampered past efforts to tackle disasters that cross Himalayan borders.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: The Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) has spent more than three decades promoting regional co-operation, including on flood early-warning systems.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: But progress has been slow.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: "There are certain highly sensitive issues in transboundary matters like comprehensive data of river flows that countries might not want to share, particularly upstream countries," says Arun Bhakta Shrestha, a former senior specialist at ICIMOD.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: He says countries should instead focus on sharing less sensitive information about disaster risks.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: "Climate change is moving the baseline itself; catching up with the previous disaster is no longer enough.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: We need to anticipate the next one," he says.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: Whether India and China are willing to take even these steps remains uncertain.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: For Nepal, the challenge is to convince its two powerful neighbours to put aside their differences and work together to tackle a shared climate threat.
sentences.article_title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

sentences.text: The group action focused on Uber's operations in London between May 2012 and March 2018 Uber has won its bid to throw out claims worth about £340m brought by thousands of London black cab drivers and two former private hire firms.
sentences.article_title: Uber wins bid to throw out £200m black cab claims

sentences.text: The claimants alleged the ride-hailing company gave Transport for London (TfL) misleading information when it first got a licence to operate in the capital in 2012.
sentences.article_title: Uber wins bid to throw out £200m black cab claims

sentences.text: But a High Court judge ruled the cases had been brought too late and dismissed them without considering whether the allegations were true.
sentences.article_title: Uber wins bid to throw out £200m black cab claims

sentences.text: Uber, which denied the claims, said it was pleased the court had thrown them out at the earliest opportunity.
sentences.article_title: Uber wins bid to throw out £200m black cab claims

sentences.text: About 13,000 drivers were seeking nearly £200m in damages, Reuters reported, while a claim on behalf of Kabbie and Iride, two private hire firms that have since closed, sought about £140m.
sentences.article_title: Uber wins bid to throw out £200m black cab claims

sentences.text: The lawsuits were filed in 2024, and Uber argued they fell outside the six-year limit for bringing such claims.
sentences.article_title: Uber wins bid to throw out £200m black cab claims

sentences.text: In a written ruling, Mr Justice Birt said the claimants could have discovered the alleged deception before 2018.
sentences.article_title: Uber wins bid to throw out £200m black cab claims

sentences.text: RGL Management, which ran the cases for the claimants, said it was very disappointed and was considering its options with the legal team.
sentences.article_title: Uber wins bid to throw out £200m black cab claims

sentences.text: Since gaining its licence, Uber has taken much of the trade once dominated by black cabs.
sentences.article_title: Uber wins bid to throw out £200m black cab claims

sentences.text: The company faces a separate case next week, when it challenges HM Revenue and Customs in a tax dispute worth more than £1bn.
