sentences.text: Online pornography depicting strangulation or incestuous relationships will be banned from early November, the government has announced.
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: From 6 November, it will be illegal to possess or publish porn which shows strangulation or suffocation, depicts sexual activity between people who are related or shows adults role-playing as children under 16 in England and Wales.
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: The new rules follow a review into porn regulation in 2025 which found depictions of choking were "rife" on popular porn sites and had helped normalise the act among young people.
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: Conservative peer Baroness Gabby Bertin, who headed the review, said the news came "not a moment too soon".
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: She told the Press Association the change in law would "send the unequivocal signal" to companies that host and facilitate porn, and also to wider society, that "extreme and violent content that encourages real-life harm is not acceptable".
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: Her independent review, commissioned by former Prime Minister Rishi Sunak's government, cited an account of a 14-year-old boy asking a teacher how to choke girls during sex .
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: It warned that people imitating such behaviour "may face devastating consequences".
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: Speaking to BBC Radio 4's Today programme on Friday, Baroness Bertin said porn showing strangulation had "absolutely sort of normalised this kind of sexual violence".
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: "That has to come to an end and I hope this law change will be the beginning of that," she said - adding that it aimed to "marry up" differences in the law about what was acceptable online and offline.
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: Non-fatal strangulation is already an offence if someone does not consent, but its depiction online is currently not illegal.
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: Amendments to the Crime and Policing Bill, which became law in April, sought to ensure such content would be captured by the legislation and made criminal offences in England and Wales.
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: Justice minister Alex Davies-Jones said it was not about "criminalising harmless sexual preferences".
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: But she said "porn can shape what people think a healthy relationship looks like, especially young people".
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: Content which "normalises, or even glorifies" violence against women can "blur the line with what is acceptable in real life", she said.
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: "If you've got this material, delete it.
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: If you're sharing it, stop," Davies-Jones added.
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: "It's not as harmless as you may think, and after 6 November, it is criminal." 'He strangled me without asking' - experts say choking during sex now normal for many The new offences each carry a maximum penalty of five years' imprisonment, for publication.
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: According to the government, this could include uploading, posting or otherwise making the content available to someone online.
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: Possession, meanwhile, could include keeping an image stored on a phone, computer or in cloud storage, the government says.
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: Someone found to be in possession of images depicting sexual activity involving a person pretending to be under 16 could face up to three years' imprisonment, after 6 November.
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: Those found to be in possession of images depicting strangulation, suffocation or penetrative sexual activity between certain relatives could face up to two years' imprisonment.
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: Porn that shows or depicts sex between step or foster-relations where one person is pretending to be under 18 will also be captured by the new offences.
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: Durham University law professor Clare McGlynn - who has previously warned widely available extreme content normalises sexual violence - welcomed the laws taking full effect.
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: "This is a potential turning point, the commencement of these laws marking a line in the sand when we decided that we were no longer going to accept the normalisation of sexually violent content in pornography," she told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: But she said questions remained over how swiftly tech platforms and regulators would act to remove and mitigate the spread of violating material.
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: "While these are criminal offences, this is not about prosecuting individuals, but transforming the online pornographic landscape and that requires the platforms and regulator to act," Prof McGlynn added.
sentences.article_title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says

sentences.text: The eagerly anticipated film, You Can See Everything, finds Holmes letting filmmakers into her California home in 2023, during the month before she began an 11-year prison sentence.

sentences.text: In You Can See Everything, Canadian comedian Fielder - known for his awkward, deadpan and at-times surreal humour, on shows including The Rehearsal and The Curse - places himself inside the action, once again blurring the lines between documentary, social experiment and prank show.
sentences.article_title: You Can See Everything seen by many on huge box office debut

sentences.article_title: You Can See Everything seen by many on huge box office debut

sentences.article_title: You Can See Everything seen by many on huge box office debut

sentences.article_title: Manifest: From reality TV to Wembley Arena in one turbulent year

sentences.text: The spokesperson added that the BBC "takes independence and transparency incredibly seriously, and we must ensure we are meeting the highest standards".

sentences.text: According to The Telegraph , external , a job advert for the 2027 secondment said a successful candidate would have "the ability to influence decision making, working with credibility and proactively with customers to share knowledge and information".
sentences.article_title: BBC pauses civil service secondment scheme

sentences.text: A now-removed blog post written by one civil servant about their placements showed a secondee describing how they had drafted copy for the news website.
sentences.article_title: BBC pauses civil service secondment scheme

sentences.text: Under the scheme, it is understood that statisticians explain data in writing that can be incorporated into stories, but they do not write the copy itself.
sentences.article_title: BBC pauses civil service secondment scheme

sentences.text: Secondees' contributions can be incorporated into journalism that scrutinises the current government, as well as all political parties.
sentences.article_title: BBC pauses civil service secondment scheme

sentences.text: The seconded statisticians also have to adhere to the Civil Service Code of Practice for Statistics.
sentences.article_title: BBC pauses civil service secondment scheme

sentences.text: It requires them to present and use data and statistics objectively and not to withhold or misrepresent data due to political or commercial influence.

sentences.text: Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma has been crowned king of Uganda's Tooro kingdom.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: The new monarch has long been a familiar face in the East African nation, where for many he was known not as the heir to the throne, but as a storyteller: a long-serving anchor and editor at the state broadcaster.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: But the 56-year-old - now King Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma Nyabongo I - has become the subject of media attention himself as his rise to the Tooro throne sparked controversy and widespread reactions beyond the country.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Tooro is one of Uganda's four main officially recognised historical kingdoms.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: For the last 31 years, it had been headed by King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, who was once known as a "boy king", after ascending to the throne as an infant.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Oyo became king in 1995 at the age of just three, following the death of his father.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Then the world's youngest monarch, he ruled until he died last month from cancer, aged just 34.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: This video can not be played King Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma Nyabongo I promised to unite his people at his coronation The coronation is a day for celebration, involving traditional practices that started at midnight.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Kijanangoma has had to perform various ceremonies and walk about 4km (2.5 miles) to the official Karuziika royal palace where he has now been crowned.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: The Tooro kingdom's Information Minister Charles Mwanguhya told the BBC Focus on Africa podcast that a mock fight would follow his crowning, to signify that kingship does not come easy.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Kijanangoma would then be blessed by members of the royal Babiito clan, he said.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: But his selection was far from straightforward.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: According to tradition, a recognised son of the late king should have succeeded him.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Close members of the royal family said Oyo had left a young son and a will with instructions that the child should be next on the throne.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: But the son has never been revealed to the public and nor was he recognised by the committee of 21 Babiito clan members who choose the king and eventually selected Kijanangoma.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: The late King Oyo was never publicly married, and little is known about his wife or their son.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Nonetheless his mother, Queen Best Kemigisa, argued that the late king's will ought to have been respected.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: However, the royal succession committee ignored her wishes, insisting their selection process was conducted in accordance with Tooro customs and traditions.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: The new king has thus found himself at the centre of a succession dispute, with Kemigisa and her close relatives unhappy with the outcome.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: The late King Oyo's mother has expressed her pain over the succession row Kemigisa referred to Kijanangoma's selection as the "announcement of a second king" being "made after the will of King Oyo was read to members of the royal family".
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: "As a mother, that was extraordinarily painful," she said, describing celebrations for the next king taking place "only metres from where my son's body lay".
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: The queen later said Oyo's son, who was in the US state of Texas, had been due to return home but that could not happen amid a "tense and polarised succession dispute".
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: "No child should be placed in circumstances where returning to his father's homeland could mean being drawn into hostility and conflict," Kemigisa asserted in a post on X.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: But according to the Tooro kingdom's information minister, the son being talked about "hasn't been presented anywhere, which means there is a growing acceptance that sad as it may be, King Oyo didn't leave a son behind".
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: While King Oyo inherited the crown from his father, Mwanguhya told the BBC "the crown has moved to a different line within the ruling clan".
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: A king must come from the Babiito clan, specifically the lineage of King George David Matthew Kamurasi Rukidi III, according to royal palace sources.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Kijanangoma and the late King Oyo are cousins.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Both are grandsons of Rukidi III, the 11th king, or Omukama, who ruled the Tooro kingdom from 1928 to 1965.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Kijanangoma was among several people who were considered for the role, including Prince George Desmond Kamurasi, who plays football for one of the UK's best-known amateur clubs .
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: After he was formally announced, Kijanangoma promised that the palace would be open to the people, while vowing to focus on unity and development.

sentences.text: "I ask you for one thing - they have given me this title as king but I cannot work alone, I have to work with you," he said.

sentences.text: President Museveni (left), who restored the traditional kingdoms in the 1990s, was pictured with Tooro's King Oyo (right) in 2010 Uganda's traditional kings have no formal political authority, but they retain cultural influence and command significant loyalty in the communities they lead.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: The country is home to four main kingdoms, the largest and most prominent being Buganda in the central region, which encompasses the capital Kampala.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: The kingdoms were abolished in 1967, but the government under President Yoweri Museveni restored them in the early 1990s.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: The government said this was to promote cultural pride and national unity, but the move has also been interpreted as a way of appeasing communities and fostering political loyalty.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Attorney General Sam Mayanja said the Tooro kingdom was cleared to go ahead with the coronation, as there had not been a formal complaint against him.

sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: "Long may he reign," he posted on X.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Kijanangoma's very name points to his royal heritage.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: His father, the first Kijanangoma, was born in the year King Rukidi III became king.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: The king gave him the name, which means the "one who comes with the royal drum".
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: The drum of royalty, foretold two generations earlier, is now returning to its bearer.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Kijanangoma was born in 1970 and raised at their family home at Kidukuru village in Fort Portal, about 300km (186 miles) from Kampala.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: He left the village to pursue further studies and graduated with a mass communication degree from Uganda's prestigious Makerere University in 1999.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: He worked as a broadcaster in a career spanning more than two decades, including in neighbouring Rwanda and at home, with the Uganda Broadcasting Corporation (UBC).
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Kijanangoma has been a journalist for much of his adult life The years spent engaging with the public, the interactions with leaders and the exposure to national affairs in his work as a journalist may yet serve him well as he returns to the community he came from, this time as their leader.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: After he was named king, Kijanangoma said he would use the connections he had built up over 21 years working as a journalist "to get good things for our people".
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: His mother, Assimwe Yusta Kijanangoma, is confident that he is well prepared for his new role.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: She says his upbringing was deeply rooted in tradition.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: "I really raised him with the teachings of the old kingdom of a cane and instructions and scolding.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: I laugh with him, and other times I scold him," she told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: She added: "Eddy is well-mannered, he does not fight, or shout, even when wronged, he says a few words and does not go so much into it." She feels good for her son, although she admits to having mixed emotions, especially as her son is taking over after the death of a "great man".

sentences.text: Kgomotso Mathekga says a lack of male role models is fuelling violence against women in his neighbourhood "I witness men hitting women all the time," says Kgomotso Mathekga, 30.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "Especially when they are both drunk." "I once had an argument with my girlfriend," he admits, "and I grabbed and slapped her." Mathekga is speaking frankly during a gathering of men aimed at helping reduce the high levels of violence against women in South Africa.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: The meeting is held in a narrow street in a Johannesburg informal settlement known as Organic Market.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: It is a maze of corrugated metal shacks and unpaved roads, close to Alexandra township.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "Now I feel pain," Mathekga continues.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We broke up and I no longer see my child.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: I feel like I've contributed to the problems in South Africa, instead of being the gentleman that I know I am." At a nearby tavern, a group of men have pulled their chairs into a circle in the dust.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: At the centre stands Itumeleng Stephen Tamaga, known locally as Bra Steve.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: The group clap and cheers.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "Listen guys," Bra Steve says.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We must stand together to fight against gender-based violence and femicide." Bra Steve is the local organiser of Father A Nation, a non-profit that works with men and boys to promote positive masculinity and help end violence against women.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: The group's meeting comes as South Africa grapples with renewed anger over renewed cases of femicide and violence against women.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: The discovery of the bodies of 12 women over three months, in the city of Ekurhuleni, near Johannesburg has reignited questions about the scale of what many people see as being a crisis of violence against women.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: Bra Steve says: "We must restore dignity to the men around here" South Africa's President Cyril Ramaphosa has acknowledged that his government has not done enough and announced measures he hopes can make women feel safer.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: The country has one of the highest murder rates in the world, with 5,427 people murdered between April and June this year alone.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: In that period, according to the South African Human Rights Commission, 569 women were killed, an average of six a day, and 1,052 others survived attempted murder.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: A report in 2022 by the Human Sciences Research Council found that more than 35% of South African women experienced physical or sexual violence, many from their own intimate partners.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: For Bra Steve, part of the solution to the crisis is helping men to understand the issue and take responsibility for their actions.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We are a lost generation," he says.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We must restore dignity to the men around here." Amongst the group of men outside the tavern is Zizipho Mtwesi, the project co-ordinator of Father A Nation.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: Reflecting on recent weeks, he says more should be done.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: The latest measures announced by Ramaphosa, including better street lighting and a review of unsolved cases , are too little, he says, and too late.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "When I think about all of these recent murders in Johannesburg, I get angry.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: Why do we have to wait for this to happen for us to act?" He looks around and gestures at the meeting.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We are trying to reach men before things like these murders happen again." Craig Wilkinson tells the group to "choose what kind of man you want to be" Craig Wilkinson is the founder of the group.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We get men to talk, to process their feelings," he explains.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "And as they do, this healing takes place.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: And the second phase is teaching and training positive masculinity.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We ultimately hope that this will eliminate the scourge of gender-based violence." He stands up, moving into the centre of the group, calling out to the men.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "You as a man are a powerful force for good," he tells them.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "You choose what kind of man you want to be.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: Women need to be safe." Father A Nation operates across South Africa, teaching healthy masculinity and running training programmes across dozens of schools and colleges.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: Mystery surrounds the spate of murders which has sparked South Africa's latest moment of soul-searching about the safety of its women.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: Police have not ruled out potential links between some of the Ekurhuleni deaths but have not said they are investigating a serial killer.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: Suspects in some of the cases have appeared in court.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: But the spate of deaths has sparked new concerns and in Organic Market some women are more fearful than ever.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: Outside a nearby shack Linkie listens with interest as she cleans clothes in a large metal bucket.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We are not safe when we are outside our place," she says.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We are afraid when we see a car behind us when we walk.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: What if this guy's going to kidnap me or do something to me?" It is a feeling shared by many women here.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: In the local hair salon, sporting a mane of thick pink braids, is Providence Maseko.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: She comes to the door to speak to Bra Steve.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: This video can not be played Women held a memorial run in Johannesburg after the discovery of Moselakgomo's body "Safety here is very bad," she says, "Maybe you are the serial killer.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: How do I know who to trust?" Bra Steve laughs.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We must talk about these things," he urges.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "Come to our meetings and we can learn to trust each other." Maseko tells me that she now takes an e-hailing taxi everywhere in the hope that it is safer.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: Back at the tavern, the men's meeting is wrapping up.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "As we try to stop gender-based violence," says Zizipho, "each and every man needs to know that they need to play a part in this.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "And if they wouldn't allow these things to happen to their own daughters or own mothers, they mustn't allow it to be done to someone else's daughter, which is their wives or their girlfriends." Mathekga is impressed with what he has heard.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "I would love them to keep on practising what we have learned, because we no longer have role models," he says.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "Our fathers and our uncles, they are there in prison.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: We must now become role models and help make this country better." Twelve women have been killed in one part of South Africa since July.

sentences.text: Ademba Allans is making it "cool" to vote in Kenya.
sentences.article_title: Making politics 'fun, trendy, sexy': How Gen Z could shape Kenya's next election

sentences.text: The student journalist turned civic mobiliser launched a voter registration drive on social media earlier this year, using snappy selfies infused with music and humour to target young people.
sentences.article_title: Making politics 'fun, trendy, sexy': How Gen Z could shape Kenya's next election

sentences.text: The result astonished him and many observers of Kenyan politics – by the time the registration period ended, 2.6 million new voters across the country had signed up.
sentences.article_title: Making politics 'fun, trendy, sexy': How Gen Z could shape Kenya's next election

sentences.text: He is aiming to get another 2.3 million on board in the next round.
sentences.article_title: Making politics 'fun, trendy, sexy': How Gen Z could shape Kenya's next election

sentences.text: "It was the Gen Z way of doing politics," he tells me.
sentences.article_title: Making politics 'fun, trendy, sexy': How Gen Z could shape Kenya's next election

sentences.text: "Fun, trendy, sexy, fashionable.
sentences.article_title: Making politics 'fun, trendy, sexy': How Gen Z could shape Kenya's next election

sentences.text: Because of how we created the hype around it, people had the fear of missing out.
sentences.article_title: Making politics 'fun, trendy, sexy': How Gen Z could shape Kenya's next election

sentences.text: Everybody wanted to be involved." Gen Z, the term used to describe people born in the late 1990s and early 2000s, burst onto the scene two years ago with mass protests that forced the government to retreat on a widely unpopular tax bill.
sentences.article_title: Making politics 'fun, trendy, sexy': How Gen Z could shape Kenya's next election

sentences.text: But their victory was followed by a police crackdown that killed and injured dozens of demonstrators.

sentences.text: The volume of oil flowing from the Middle East region has almost returned to pre-war levels, data shows, despite the continued restrictions Iran is placing on vessels attempting to travel through the Strait of Hormuz.

sentences.text: Seven months after the US-Israel war with Iran led to the effective closure of the critical waterway, the maritime intelligence firm Kpler said that in the final week of September, daily oil flow from the Middle East reached 92% of its pre-war baseline.

sentences.text: About 40% of the total oil exported from the region in September bypassed the strait and exited via overland pipelines to ports on the Red Sea or the Gulf of Oman, up from 17% before the war, according to Kpler.

sentences.text: The US military has been supporting ships as they pass through the Strait of Hormuz since at least mid-June and US Navy data shows the number of vessels assisted by US forces is up by a third in September compared with August.

sentences.text: Martin Kelly, senior intelligence analyst at security firm EOS Risk Group, told BBC Verify that US support is primarily in the form of "air support to ships", including through issuing warnings and intercepting incoming threats from drones, missiles or boats.

sentences.text: But ships moving through the US-recommended southern route of the strait near the coast of Oman, rather than seeking permission to use Iran's northern route, continue to be targeted.

sentences.text: September saw the highest number of successful Iranian attacks on commercial shipping since March, according to the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data conflict monitor.

sentences.text: Naveen Das, a senior oil analyst from Kpler, said the oil market "doesn't trust that we're going stay in this status quo" because of the geopolitical risk of further Iranian escalation and the possible impact of the US midterm elections.

sentences.text: Most of the oil passing through the strait now moves via a "shuttle system" of more than 60 large oil tankers moving back and forth, according to Kpler.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: More than 70% of the crude oil which passed through the strait in August was transferred from these "shuttle tankers" onto other vessels in the Gulf of Oman, Kpler said.

sentences.text: BBC Verify has analysed satellite imagery which appears to show these ship-to-ship transfers, taking place off the coast of the Omani port city, Sohar.

sentences.text: Imagery taken on 24 September shows six pairs of ships docked or paired together near the port, seemingly more protected from Iranian attack.

sentences.text: But there is "a question over how long these ships can last", said Martin Kelly, particularly as attacks on them continue.

sentences.text: An average of more than four million barrels of oil per day was transferred from ship to ship in the Gulf of Oman over in the week to 30 September, according to Kpler.

sentences.text: Overall, an average of 12 million barrels of oil per day passed through the strait over this period, compared with a pre-war baseline of 17 million.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: Oil exporting countries in the Gulf have also responded to Iranian attacks in the Strait of Hormuz by exporting more crude oil overland via pipelines.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: Just under 20% of crude is now leaving the region from ports on the Red Sea at the end of Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline, which is recording exports of more than four million barrels per day, according to Kpler.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: Three weeks after an attack on this pipeline blamed on Iran-backed proxies in Iraq, Saudi Arabia is now exporting through the pipeline at "full stretch", according to Kpler.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: Almost a quarter of all crude flowing from the region is now being piped past the Strait of Hormuz to terminals along the Gulf of Oman, particularly the city of Fujairah in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Kpler's data shows.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: Naveen Das from Kpler said this increased use of pipelines is likely to become the "new normal" because "it seems very improbable that we live in a world whereby the Gulf countries and Iran go back to being relatively harmonious".

sentences.text: Oil exports from Iran have fallen almost to zero following the re-imposition of a US blockade in mid-July, down from 1.7 million barrels a day before the war began, Kpler data shows.

sentences.text: While crude oil flow from the Middle East has resumed to almost normal levels, exports of liquified natural gas and oil products like jet fuel and have remained well below pre-conflict volumes.

Her organisation, like Hope Dealers in Columbus, distributes test strips which check drugs for fentanyl, medetomidine, xylazine and other adulterants.

sentences.text: Karen, a recovery worker, tends to a gaunt-looking man in a wheelchair in an upscale part of town Dart has been sheriff of Cook County for 20 years, so I ask him how the war on drugs was progressing.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: "I don't think there's anybody involved with it who would sit there and say it's a raging success.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: And the new problem, he says, reiterating the Chicago drug dealer, is synthetics.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: "The tradition has always been that law enforcement had an even more vital role because everything that was potent was coming across the border, whether it was coming from Colombia, Mexico, China, the poppy fields of Afghanistan.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: Now, with the explosion of synthetic drugs, people can do this in their house, in their sink, in their bathtub, you name it." Victory in the war on drugs won't come from focusing just on the supply side, the sheriff adds.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: "Front and centre there's got to be huge substance abuse treatment," he says, mentioning a number of recovery programmes running in his jail.
sentences.article_title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

sentences.text: "You can reduce the market if you can address people's issues with substance abuse.

sentences.text: And I know many people who, after long struggles, have come out on the other side in a really good way." Karen knows how difficult it is to quit.

sentences.text: You know, it's not worth it to get high for like a couple of hours." She continues: "There's a lot of people are struggling, especially that our country is raising our prices, raising the prices on food and it's causing it.

sentences.text: A lot of mental health now is very expensive so people can't get help, and one way they can turn to that is by drugs." Generations of Americans have endured the drugs crisis, but it is never the same crisis.
